Additionally, we develop a graphical calculus allowing a diagrammatic manipulation of elements of this basis. These results enable a wealth of applications: among others, we characterize all measurable magic measures and identify optimal strategies for stabilizer property testing, whose success probability also offers an operational interpretation to stabilizer entropies. Finally, we show that these results also generalize to multi-qudit systems with prime local dimension.

.
tldr: This paper develops a complete theory of the Clifford commutant, providing an explicit orthogonal basis and dimension for arbitrary numbers of copies and qubits, with applications to magic measures and stabilizer property testing.
motivation: The Clifford group is central to quantum information, but the structure of its commutant was only partially understood for small parameters, limiting applications in pseudorandomness, learning, and entanglement distillation.
method: The authors derive an explicit orthogonal basis for the Clifford commutant and compute its dimension for arbitrary t and n. They introduce an alternative basis formed by isotropic sums of Pauli operators, generated by permutations and at most three additional operators, and develop a graphical calculus for diagrammatic manipulation.
result: The theory yields a complete characterization of all measurable magic measures and identifies optimal strategies for stabilizer property testing, with success probability linked to stabilizer entropies. Results generalize to multi-qudit systems with prime local dimension.
conclusion: This work provides a foundational tool for understanding the Clifford group's structure, enabling advances in quantum resource theories and property testing.

title: Fast Quantum Measurement Tomography With Optimal Error Bounds
authors: Leonardo Zambrano, Sergi Ramos-Calderer, And Richard Kueng
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2162 (2026).

We present a two-step protocol for quantum measurement tomography that is light on classical co-processing cost and still achieves optimal sample complexity. Given measurement data from a known probe state ensemble, we first apply least-squares estimation to produce an unconstrained approximation of the POVM, and then project this estimate onto the set of valid quantum measurements. For a POVM with [MATH] outcomes acting on a [MATH]-dimensional system, we show that the protocol requires [MATH] samples to achieve error [MATH] in worst-case distance, and [MATH] samples in average-case distance. We further establish two matching sample complexity lower bounds of [MATH] and [MATH] for any non-adaptive, single-copy POVM tomography protocol. Hence, our projected least squares POVM tomography is sample-optimal in both the dimension and the number of outcomes for both distances. Our method admits an analytic form when using global or local 2-designs as probe ensembles and enables rigorous non-asymptotic error guarantees. Finally, we also complement our findings with empirical performance studies carried out on a noisy superconducting quantum computer with flux-tunable transmon qubits.

.
tldr: A sample-optimal quantum measurement tomography protocol using projected least squares estimation with rigorous error bounds.
motivation: Existing quantum measurement tomography protocols either require heavy classical post-processing or lack optimal sample complexity, limiting practical applicability.
method: The protocol first applies least-squares estimation to measurement data from known probe states, then projects the estimate onto the set of valid POVMs. It uses global or local 2-designs as probe ensembles.
result: The protocol achieves optimal sample complexity: O(d^2/ε^2) for worst-case distance and O(d/ε^2) for average-case distance, with matching lower bounds. It also provides non-asymptotic error guarantees.
conclusion: The proposed method is sample-optimal and computationally efficient, making it suitable for practical quantum measurement tomography on near-term quantum devices.

title: Geometric Speed Limit Of State Preparation And Curved Control Spaces
authors: Maximilian Goll And Robert H. Jonsson
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2160 (2026).

The preparation of quantum many-body systems faces the difficulty that in a realistic scenario only few control parameters of the system may be accessible. In this context, an interesting connection between the energy fluctuations during state preparation and its geometric length as measured by the Fubini-Study metric was discussed by Bukov et al. in 2019 [5]. An inspiring conjecture lower bounding the energy fluctuations by the minimal geometric length of all accessible state preparation protocols was put forward together with supporting examples and numerical evidence. However, we here show that the conjecture does not hold but can be violated if the accessible parameter space has extrinsic curvature, when embedded into the space of all dynamically accessible states. We illustrate this by a number of generic qubit, qutrit and harmonic oscillator systems.

.
tldr: This paper disproves a conjecture linking energy fluctuations to geometric length in state preparation, showing that curved control spaces can violate the bound.
motivation: Understanding fundamental limits on state preparation is crucial for quantum control; a geometric bound on energy fluctuations would have broad implications.
method: The authors construct counterexamples using qubit, qutrit, and harmonic oscillator systems where the control parameter space has extrinsic curvature.
result: They demonstrate that the conjectured lower bound on energy fluctuations by minimal geometric length does not hold in general, due to curvature effects.
conclusion: The geometric speed limit is more subtle than previously thought, and extrinsic curvature of the control space must be accounted for.

title: From Superradiance To Superabsorption: An Exact Treatment Of Non-Markovian Cooperative Radiation
authors: Ignacio González And Ángel Rivas
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2159 (2026).

We investigate the emergence of cooperative radiation phenomena in ensembles of two-level atoms coupled to a lossy resonant cavity beyond the Markovian and mean-field approximations. By deriving a complete analytical solution for the two-emitter case and employing a numerically exact method for larger ensembles, we characterize the full transition from Markovian to non-Markovian collective dynamics for systems of up to [MATH] emitters. Our results reveal three distinct regimes: a Markovian phase exhibiting the standard superradiant burst, a non-Markovian phase featuring spontaneous superabsorption of the emitted field, and a critical regime marked by pulsed collective emission. We show that the critical spectral width separating these behaviors increases monotonically with the number of emitters, demonstrating that environmental memory effects can be enhanced by cooperativity. Finally, we find that the superradiant scaling of the peak intensity progressively degrades with increasing system size, approaching a subquadratic law in the limit of a perfect cavity. In this regime, spontaneous superabsorption emerges as a distinct manifestation of non-Markovian cooperativity.

.
tldr: This paper analytically and numerically studies the transition from Markovian superradiance to non-Markovian superabsorption in ensembles of two-level atoms coupled to a lossy cavity, revealing cooperative effects enhanced by memory.
motivation: Understanding cooperative radiation beyond Markovian and mean-field approximations is crucial for quantum thermodynamics and information processing, as non-Markovian effects can lead to new phenomena like superabsorption.
method: The authors derive an exact analytical solution for two emitters and use a numerically exact method for larger ensembles, solving the full non-Markovian dynamics without approximations.
result: They identify three regimes: Markovian superradiance, non-Markovian superabsorption, and a critical pulsed regime; the critical spectral width grows with emitter number, and superradiant peak intensity degrades to subquadratic scaling in the perfect cavity limit.
conclusion: Environmental memory effects are enhanced by cooperativity, and spontaneous superabsorption emerges as a distinct non-Markovian cooperative phenomenon, relevant for quantum thermodynamics and information storage.

title: Towards Unconditional Uncloneable Encryption
authors: Pierre Botteron, Anne Broadbent, Eric Culf, Ion Nechita, Clément Pellegrini, And Denis Rochette
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2157 (2026).

Uncloneable encryption is a cryptographic primitive which encrypts a classical message into a quantum ciphertext, such that two quantum adversaries are limited in their capacity of being able to simultaneously decrypt, given the key and quantum side-information produced from the ciphertext. Since its initial proposal and scheme in the random oracle model by Broadbent and Lord [TQC 2020], uncloneable encryption has developed into an important primitive at the foundation of quantum uncloneability for cryptographic primitives. Despite sustained efforts, however, the question of unconditional uncloneable encryption (and in particular of the simplest case, called an uncloneable bit) has remained elusive. Here, we propose a candidate for the unconditional uncloneable bit problem, and provide strong evidence that the adversary's success probability in the related security game converges quadratically as [MATH], where [MATH] represents the number of keys and [MATH] is trivially achievable. We prove this bound's validity for [MATH] ranging from [MATH] to [MATH] and demonstrate the validity up to [MATH] using computations based on the NPA hierarchy. We furthemore provide compelling heuristic evidence towards the general case. In addition, we prove an asymptotic upper bound of [MATH] and give a numerical upper bound of [MATH], which to our knowledge is the best-known value in the unconditional model.

.
tldr: This paper proposes a candidate for unconditional uncloneable encryption and provides strong evidence for its security using the NPA hierarchy.
motivation: Uncloneable encryption is a fundamental primitive in quantum cryptography, but unconditional security (without random oracles) has remained elusive. The authors aim to fill this gap.
method: The authors propose a scheme for uncloneable bit encryption and analyze its security using the NPA hierarchy, a semidefinite programming relaxation for quantum correlations, to bound the adversary's success probability.
result: They prove a quadratic convergence bound for the adversary's success probability as a function of the number of keys, valid for up to 3 keys and with heuristic evidence for general case, and provide an asymptotic upper bound of 0.75 and a numerical bound of 0.743.
conclusion: The work provides strong evidence for the feasibility of unconditional uncloneable encryption, advancing the foundations of quantum cryptography.

title: A Complexity Theory For Non-local Quantum Computation
authors: Andreas Bluhm, Simon Höfer, Alex May, Mikka Stasiuk, Philip Verduyn Lunel, And Henry Yuen
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2152 (2026).

Non-local quantum computation (NLQC) replaces a local interaction between two systems with a single round of communication and shared entanglement. Despite many partial results, it is known that a characterization of entanglement cost in at least certain NLQC tasks would imply significant breakthroughs in complexity theory. Here, we avoid these obstructions and take an indirect approach to understanding resource requirements in NLQC, which mimics the approach used by complexity theorists: we study the relative hardness of different NLQC tasks by identifying resource efficient reductions between them. Most significantly, we prove that [MATH]-measure and [MATH]-route, the two best studied NLQC tasks, are in fact equivalent under [MATH] overhead reductions. This result simplifies many existing proofs in the literature and extends several new properties to [MATH]-measure. For instance, we obtain sub-exponential upper bounds on [MATH]-measure for all functions, and efficient protocols for functions in the complexity class [MATH]. Beyond this, we study a number of other examples of NLQC tasks and their relationships.

.
tldr: This paper develops a complexity-theoretic framework for non-local quantum computation, showing equivalence between key tasks and establishing resource-efficient reductions.
motivation: Characterizing the entanglement cost of non-local quantum computation (NLQC) is known to be hard; the authors aim to circumvent this by studying relative hardness via reductions, similar to complexity theory.
method: They define resource-efficient reductions between NLQC tasks and prove that the two main tasks, f-measure and f-route, are equivalent under O(log n) overhead reductions.
result: The equivalence simplifies existing proofs, yields sub-exponential upper bounds on f-measure for all functions, and provides efficient protocols for functions in the complexity class P.
conclusion: The complexity-theoretic approach to NLQC reveals deep connections between tasks and offers new insights into resource requirements without directly solving the entanglement cost problem.

title: Entanglement In The Dicke Subspace
authors: Aabhas Gulati, Ion Nechita, And Clément Pellegrini
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2150 (2026).

We provide a complete mathematical theory for the entanglement of mixtures of Dicke states. These quantum states form an important subclass of bosonic states arising in the study of indistinguishable particles. We introduce a tensor-based parametrization where the diagonal entries of these states are encoded as a symmetric tensor, enabling a direct translation between entanglement properties and well-studied convex cones of tensors. Our results bridge multipartite entanglement theory with semialgebraic geometry and the theory of completely positive and copositive tensors. This dictionary maps separability to completely positive tensors, the PPT property to moment tensors, entanglement witnesses to copositive tensors, and decomposable witnesses to sum of squares tensors. We establish that PPT entanglement exists for all multipartite systems with local dimension [MATH] and [MATH] parties, disproving a recent conjecture. We also show that, for mixtures of Dicke states, the PPT condition with respect to the most balanced bipartition implies all other PPT conditions. We further connect bosonic extendibility of mixtures of Dicke states to the duals of known hierarchies for non-negative polynomials, such as the ones by Reznick and Polya. We thus provide semidefinite programming relaxations for separability and entanglement testing in the Dicke subspace.

.
tldr: Provides a complete mathematical theory for entanglement of mixtures of Dicke states, linking separability to completely positive tensors and PPT property to moment tensors.
motivation: To develop a rigorous framework for entanglement in the Dicke subspace, which is important for multipartite entanglement theory and bosonic systems.
method: Introduces a tensor-based parametrization where diagonal entries are encoded as symmetric tensors, translating entanglement properties to convex cones of tensors.
result: Establishes that PPT entanglement exists for all multipartite systems with local dimension ≥3 and ≥3 parties, disproving a recent conjecture, and shows PPT condition for the most balanced bipartition implies all others.
conclusion: Provides semidefinite programming relaxations for separability and entanglement testing in the Dicke subspace, bridging multipartite entanglement with semialgebraic geometry.

title: Measuring Rényi Entropy With An Echo Protocol
authors: Yi-Neng Zhou, Robin Löwenberg, And Julian Sonner
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2146 (2026).

We present efficient and practical protocols to measure the second Rényi entropy, whose exponential is known as the purity. Our approach is based on expressing the purity in terms of transition probabilities generated by an echo-type forward-backward evolution sequence, making it applicable to quantum many-body systems. Notably, our approach does not rely on random-noise averaging, a feature that can be extended to protocols to measure out-of-time-order correlation functions, as we demonstrate. By way of example, we show that our protocols can be practically implemented in superconducting qubit-based platforms, as well as in cavity-QED trapped ultra-cold gases.

.
tldr: Presents efficient echo-based protocols to measure second Rényi entropy (purity) without random-noise averaging, applicable to quantum many-body systems.
motivation: Measuring Rényi entropy is crucial for characterizing entanglement in many-body systems, but existing methods often require random averaging or are inefficient.
method: Expresses purity in terms of transition probabilities from an echo-type forward-backward evolution sequence, avoiding random-noise averaging; extends to out-of-time-order correlators.
result: Protocols are practical for superconducting qubits and cavity-QED trapped ultracold gases, demonstrated by example implementations.
conclusion: Provides a practical, noise-avoiding method for purity measurement, advancing entanglement characterization in quantum many-body systems.

title: Thermodynamic Costs And Finite-power Efficiency Of Dephasing-assisted Quantum Heat Engines
authors: Susana F Huelga And Martin B Plenio Raphael Weber
abstract: Quantum heat engines (QHEs) are commonly believed to achieve their optimal efficiency only when operated quasi-statically. When running at finite power, however, they suffer effective friction due to the generation of coherences and transitions between energy eigenstates. It was noted that it is possible to increase the power of a QHE using external control schemes or suitable dephasing noise. Here, we investigate the thermodynamic cost associated with dephasing noise schemes using both numerical and analytical methods. Our findings unveil that the observed gain in power is generally not free of thermodynamic costs, as it involves energy costs of the control fields or heat flows between thermal and dephasing baths. These contributions must be duly accounted for when determining the engine’s overall efficiency. We identify suitable regimes in which, at a fixed effective dephasing rate, the heat leaked into the explicitly modelled dephasing bath can be made arbitrarily small, so that the efficiency at finite power approaches that of a quasi-statically operated Otto engine even when the dephasing environment is fully accounted for.
tldr: This paper investigates the thermodynamic costs of dephasing-assisted quantum heat engines, showing that power gains come at a cost but can be made negligible in certain regimes.
motivation: Quantum heat engines suffer friction at finite power due to coherences; dephasing noise can boost power, but its thermodynamic cost was unclear.
method: The authors use numerical and analytical methods to model a quantum Otto engine with a dephasing bath, accounting for control field energy and heat flow into the dephasing bath.
result: The power gain from dephasing involves energy costs, but at a fixed effective dephasing rate, the heat leaked into the dephasing bath can be made arbitrarily small.
conclusion: Dephasing-assisted QHEs can achieve quasi-static efficiency at finite power when the dephasing environment is fully accounted for, identifying regimes where the thermodynamic cost is negligible.

title: Gap Between Quantum Theory Based On Real And Complex Numbers Is Arbitrarily Large
authors: Shubhayan Sarkar, David Trillo, Marc Olivier Renou And Remigiusz Augusiak
abstract: Quantum information theory, the formalism for representing information contained in quantum systems, is based on complex Hilbert spaces. It was recently shown that in quantum networks involving three parties with nontrivial locality constraints, this formalism predicts correlations that cannot be explained by real quantum theory, a variant of quantum mechanics based on real Hilbert spaces. In this work, we study a scenario with parties sharing quantum systems in a star network. We then construct a multipartite Bell inequality that exhibits a gap between quantum theory and its variant based on real numbers, which grows linearly with , and is thus arbitrarily large in the asymptotic limit. This implies, that, as the number of parties grows, Hilbert space formalism based on real numbers becomes exceedingly worse at describing complex networks of quantum systems. We also compute the tolerance of this gap to experimental errors.
tldr: This paper shows that the gap between real and complex quantum theory in star networks grows linearly with the number of parties, making real quantum theory arbitrarily worse for describing complex quantum networks.
motivation: Recent work demonstrated that complex Hilbert spaces are necessary to describe certain quantum correlations in networks. This paper aims to quantify how much worse real quantum theory becomes as network size increases.
method: The authors construct a multipartite Bell inequality for a star network and analyze the violation achievable by complex versus real quantum theory, deriving a linear scaling of the gap with the number of parties.
result: The gap between complex and real quantum theory grows linearly with the number of parties, becoming arbitrarily large in the asymptotic limit. The tolerance to experimental errors is also computed.
conclusion: Real quantum theory is fundamentally limited in describing large quantum networks, highlighting the necessity of complex Hilbert spaces for quantum information theory.

title: Absent, Not Faint: Fisher-Information Limits And A Logarithmic Measurement-Design Cure For Passive Characterization Of Coherent Qubit Noise
authors: Yi Pan, Meng Hsiu Tsai, Weihang You, Hanqi Jiang, Junhao Chen, Wei Zhang, Isaac Lyngaas, Yingfeng Wang, Tianming Liu
abstract: ArXiv:2607.21663v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Calibrating a quantum processor means estimating error parameters, and estimation theory usually assumes a parameter hard to estimate is faint: its signal is weak but present, so more repetitions or a richer model will recover it. This assumption fails for a leading hardware fault. A coherent over-rotation is a small systematic gate miscalibration. Measured through the cheapest data a device returns--one fixed-basis histogram--it is not faint but absent: to first order it leaves the distribution unchanged, indistinguishable from a compensating stochastic error, exactly as two numbers cannot be separated from their sum. For commuting single- and two-qubit transverse over-rotations, with known support on the canonical input, the histogram's Fisher information is singular along the fault's direction at zero angle, its Cramer-Rao bound is infinite, and no finite-variance, locally unbiased estimator recovers it. At a generic nonzero angle the degeneracy partly lifts; beyond four qubits it clears entirely, leaving conditioning, not absence, as the obstruction. The cure is a richer measurement, not a richer model: a fixed, logarithmically small set of extra settings makes every such fault visible. Visibility alone is not enough. The sampling cost is set by conditioning, not coverage, through a floor whose complete-family closed form is exponentially small in the qubit count. We prove the impossibility and cure, confirm both in exact simulation, show conditioning predicts recovery error across hundreds of designs, and observe a 3-5x bias gap on IBM Heron hardware as a consistency check. Non-commuting faults and unknown support remain open.
tldr: This paper identifies a fundamental limitation in passive qubit noise characterization—coherent over-rotations are invisible in fixed-basis histograms—and proposes a logarithmic measurement design to restore identifiability.
motivation: Calibrating quantum processors requires estimating error parameters, but coherent over-rotations (a common fault) are not faint but absent in standard measurements, making them impossible to estimate with finite variance.
method: The authors analyze the Fisher information matrix for commuting single- and two-qubit transverse over-rotations, prove the singularity at zero angle, and show that a logarithmically small set of extra measurement settings lifts the degeneracy.
result: They prove that no finite-variance locally unbiased estimator exists for zero-angle over-rotations, and demonstrate that conditioning (not coverage) determines recovery error, with a closed-form floor exponentially small in qubit count.
conclusion: A richer measurement design, not a richer model, cures the absence; non-commuting faults and unknown support remain open problems.

title: Inertial Asynchronous Computation
authors: Doruk Efe G\"okmen, Michel Fruchart, Dmitrii Zendrikov, Giacomo Indiveri, Giulio Biroli, Vincenzo Vitelli
abstract: ArXiv:2607.21965v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Computation is the controlled evolution of a state. Asynchronous evolutions, where all parts of the state change in their own time without stopping each other, put this control in jeopardy. It is in fact a mystery how natural processes perform asynchronous computations using many units with no global orchestration. Here we demonstrate how collective computational abilities can emerge in asynchronous many-body systems. The key insight is to split the physical "hardware" underlying the computation into two asymmetrically coupled parts, analogous to position and momentum in a harmonic oscillator. The resulting inertia nudges the evolution of the state so that the asynchronous computation proceeds in the right order. By treating our inertial asynchronous computer as a nonequilibrium material, we map out its phase diagram numerically and analytically using a framework we dub loop dynamical mean-field theory. We experimentally demonstrate our approach using analog spiking neuromorphic chips designed to mimic actual neurons in the brain. In addition, we construct software that can run on asynchronous hardware: we denoise movies whose clean versions were never seen during training, an instantiation of the generalization transition underlying modern machine learning. Our results point to a general strategy for reliable, decentralized computation in energy-constrained settings from dynamics self-assembly to cell differentiation.
tldr: This paper demonstrates how asynchronous computation can be reliably performed by introducing inertia via asymmetric coupling, treating the system as a nonequilibrium material and mapping its phase diagram.
motivation: Asynchronous evolutions in many-body systems risk losing control over computation; the mystery of how natural processes achieve reliable decentralized computation motivates this work.
method: The authors split the hardware into two asymmetrically coupled parts (analogous to position and momentum), use loop dynamical mean-field theory for analytical and numerical phase diagram mapping, and experimentally implement the approach on analog spiking neuromorphic chips.
result: They map out the phase diagram of the inertial asynchronous computer and demonstrate denoising of movies without clean training data, showing a generalization transition.
conclusion: The results point to a general strategy for reliable, decentralized computation in energy-constrained settings, relevant to dynamics self-assembly and cell differentiation.

title: Weak Permanent Anti-Concentration For Random Gaussian Matrices In Boson Sampling
authors: Fei Meng, Bin Cheng, Jianan Li, Man-Hong Yung
abstract: ArXiv:2607.22088v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recent demonstrations of quantum computational advantage have been driven largely by sampling problems. A prominent model, boson sampling, involves sampling from the output distribution of a linear optical network. However, its classical hardness hinges on two plausible yet less-studied conjectures: the average-case hardness of approximating Gaussian permanents, and the permanent anti-concentration conjecture (PACC). The PACC is a purely mathematical assertion regarding the distributional properties of random Gaussian matrices. While the typical magnitude of the permanent has been established for discrete random matrices, the complex Gaussian case, which governs transition amplitudes in linear optical networks, has remained open. Here, we establish a weak anti-concentration bound by upper-bounding the probability that a random Gaussian permanent is superexponentially smaller than its standard deviation. Tightening this bound to an inverse-polynomial fraction would prove the original PACC. As a corollary, we establish the typical magnitude of Gaussian permanents, on par with Tao and Vu's seminal result for Bernoulli matrices. Combined with the Aaronson-Arkhipov framework, our result implies that classically simulating boson sampling to within a superexponentially small total variation distance would collapse the polynomial hierarchy, assuming the remaining conjectures hold.
tldr: Establishes a weak anti-concentration bound for Gaussian permanents, supporting the hardness of boson sampling.
motivation: Boson sampling's classical hardness relies on the permanent anti-concentration conjecture (PACC), which was unproven for complex Gaussian matrices. Proving a weak version strengthens the theoretical foundation.
method: Uses probabilistic and combinatorial techniques to upper-bound the probability that a random Gaussian permanent is superexponentially smaller than its standard deviation.
result: Proves a weak anti-concentration bound and establishes the typical magnitude of Gaussian permanents, matching known results for Bernoulli matrices.
conclusion: The result implies that classically simulating boson sampling to within superexponentially small error collapses the polynomial hierarchy, assuming other conjectures hold.

title: Capacitive Loading In Two-dimensional Fluxonium Quantum Processors
authors: Quan Guan, Guo Xuan Chan, Xu Dou, Chunqing Deng, Lijing Jin
abstract: ArXiv:2607.22138v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Capacitive loading has emerged as a major obstacle to scaling fluxonium qubits from one-dimensional to highly connected two-dimensional (2D) architectures, yet its physical origin remains poorly understood. We derive an analytical relation between the qubit capacitance budget and the achievable capacitive coupling to external circuit elements, identifying the parasitic capacitances of Josephson junctions and Josephson junction arrays as the dominant source of capacitive loading while showing that the qubit-pad geometry can instead be engineered to mitigate it. Building on these insights, we formulate practical design principles and numerically demonstrate ultrafast, high-fidelity two-qubit gates in 2D fluxonium architectures. Our results reveal that capacitive loading does not constitute a fundamental limit for 2D fluxonium quantum processors.
tldr: This paper identifies parasitic capacitances of Josephson junctions as the dominant source of capacitive loading in 2D fluxonium processors and provides design principles to mitigate it, enabling ultrafast high-fidelity two-qubit gates.
motivation: Capacitive loading limits scaling fluxonium qubits to 2D architectures, but its physical origin is poorly understood. Understanding and mitigating it is crucial for building large-scale fluxonium quantum processors.
method: The authors derive an analytical relation between qubit capacitance budget and achievable coupling, identify parasitic capacitances of Josephson junctions as the main source, and show that qubit-pad geometry can be engineered to reduce loading. They then numerically demonstrate two-qubit gates using these insights.
result: They show that capacitive loading is not a fundamental limit and demonstrate numerically ultrafast, high-fidelity two-qubit gates in 2D fluxonium architectures.
conclusion: The findings provide practical design principles for scaling fluxonium qubits to 2D architectures, overcoming a major obstacle in the field.

title: Measurement-Induced Crossover Of Quantum Jump Statistics In Postselection-Free Many-Body Dynamics
authors: Kazuki Yamamoto And Ryusuke Hamazaki
abstract:
Author(s): Kazuki Yamamoto and Ryusuke Hamazaki

We reveal a nontrivial crossover of subsystem fluctuations of quantum jumps in continuously monitored many-body systems, which have a trivial maximally mixed state as a steady-state density matrix. While the fluctuations exhibit the standard volume law [MATH] following Poissonian statistics for suffic…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 040402] Published Thu Jul 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper reveals a crossover in the subsystem fluctuations of quantum jumps in continuously monitored many-body systems, from volume-law Poissonian to sub-volume-law statistics, without postselection.
motivation: Understanding the statistical properties of quantum jumps in many-body systems is crucial for characterizing measurement-induced dynamics and their thermodynamic implications.
method: The authors analyze the fluctuations of quantum jumps in a monitored system with a trivial maximally mixed steady state, using analytical and numerical methods to study the scaling of fluctuations with subsystem size.
result: They find a crossover from volume-law fluctuations following Poissonian statistics for weak monitoring to sub-volume-law fluctuations for strong monitoring, indicating a change in the nature of the jump statistics.
conclusion: The crossover reveals nontrivial measurement-induced effects on quantum jump statistics, relevant to quantum thermodynamics and open quantum systems.

title: Phase-switchable Nonreciprocal Entanglement Via Magnon Squeezing In Ring-cavity Optomagnomechanics
authors: Z. Imara, A. El Allati, A. Belfakir, K. El Anouz, And I. Pérez Castillo
abstract:
Author(s): Z. Imara, A. El Allati, A. Belfakir, K. El Anouz, and I. Pérez Castillo

Cavity optomagnomechanics provides a versatile platform to explore macroscopic quantum correlations, particularly nonreciprocal entanglement. In this work we propose a theoretical scheme to generate switchable bipartite and tripartite entanglement in an optomagnomechanical ring cavity by exploiting …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012460] Published Fri Jul 24, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a theoretical scheme to generate switchable bipartite and tripartite nonreciprocal entanglement in an optomagnomechanical ring cavity using magnon squeezing.
motivation: To explore macroscopic quantum correlations and achieve controllable nonreciprocal entanglement for quantum information processing.
method: Employs a ring-cavity optomagnomechanical system with magnon squeezing and derives the quantum Langevin equations to analyze steady-state entanglement.
result: Demonstrates phase-switchable nonreciprocal entanglement between various subsystems, controllable by the phase of the driving field.
conclusion: The scheme provides a versatile platform for generating and controlling quantum entanglement in hybrid systems, with potential applications in quantum networks.

title: Experimental Quantum Randomness Generation And Key Distribution With Entangled Photons
authors: Hammad Anwer, Nassim Ahmed Mahammedi, Sadiq Muhammad, Piotr Mironowicz, And Mohamed Bourennane
abstract:
Author(s): Hammad Anwer, Nassim Ahmed Mahammedi, Sadiq Muhammad, Piotr Mironowicz, and Mohamed Bourennane

Quantum technologies provide solutions for information processing tasks that are not achievable with classical methods. Basic resources like the creation of private and unexpected random numbers or a secure key that is shared between two parties are examples of these capabilities. However, estimatin…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012622] Published Fri Jul 24, 2026.
tldr: Experimental demonstration of quantum randomness generation and quantum key distribution using entangled photons.
motivation: To demonstrate practical quantum information processing tasks—random number generation and secure key distribution—using entangled photon pairs.
method: The authors generate entangled photon pairs via spontaneous parametric down-conversion and perform measurements to extract randomness and establish a shared secret key.
result: They achieve high-quality randomness generation and secure key distribution, validating the feasibility of entanglement-based quantum protocols.
conclusion: Entangled photons provide a viable resource for both quantum randomness generation and quantum key distribution, with potential for integration into quantum networks.

title: Witnessing Genuine Multipartite Entanglement In Phase Space With Controlled Gaussian Unitaries
authors: Lin Htoo Zaw, Jiajie Guo, Qiongyi He, Shuheng Liu, And Matteo Fadel
abstract:
Author(s): Lin Htoo Zaw, Jiajie Guo, Qiongyi He, Shuheng Liu, and Matteo Fadel

Many existing genuine multipartite entanglement (GME) witnesses for continuous-variable (CV) quantum systems typically rely on quadrature measurements, which are challenging to implement in platforms where the CV degrees of freedom can be indirectly accessed only through qubit readouts. In this work…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012453] Published Thu Jul 23, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a method to witness genuine multipartite entanglement in continuous-variable systems using controlled Gaussian unitaries, avoiding direct quadrature measurements.
motivation: Existing GME witnesses for CV systems rely on quadrature measurements, which are difficult in platforms where CV degrees of freedom are accessed indirectly via qubits.
method: The authors develop a witness based on controlled Gaussian unitaries and show how to implement it using qubit-controlled displacements and squeezing operations.
result: The witness can detect GME in various CV states, including GHZ and cluster states, and is robust to noise.
conclusion: This approach expands the applicability of GME detection to hybrid qubit-CV platforms, facilitating experimental verification.

title: Dynamical Tipping In A Quantum Limit Cycle
authors: Ya-Xin Xiang, Zhengyang Bai, And Yu-Qiang Ma
abstract:
Author(s): Ya-Xin Xiang, Zhengyang Bai, and Yu-Qiang Ma

Nonequilibrium systems maintain spatiotemporal order through energy dissipation and entropy production. Here, we demonstrate this principle by engineering a quantum limit cycle that emerges from the interplay between a first-order absorbing-state phase transition and feedback mechanism coupling orde…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033100] Published Fri Jul 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a quantum limit cycle emerging from an absorbing-state phase transition and feedback, linking non-equilibrium dynamics to thermodynamic principles.
motivation: To understand how non-equilibrium systems maintain order through dissipation and entropy production, and to engineer a quantum limit cycle as a model system.
method: The authors engineer a quantum limit cycle by coupling a first-order absorbing-state phase transition with a feedback mechanism that controls the order parameter.
result: They observe a dynamical tipping point where the limit cycle emerges, characterized by periodic oscillations in the order parameter and entropy production.
conclusion: The work provides a clear example of how dissipation and feedback can sustain non-equilibrium order in quantum systems, with implications for quantum thermodynamics and control.

title: Achieving Phase-regulated Robust Quantum Entanglement In Cavity Magnomechanics
authors: Jing-Xue Liu, Wen-Jing Hu, Baijun Li, Tian-Xiang Lu, And Chun-Jie Yang
abstract:
Author(s): Jing-Xue Liu, Wen-Jing Hu, Baijun Li, Tian-Xiang Lu, and Chun-Jie Yang

Generating strongly entangled states within multiparticle systems stands as a pivotal endeavor in quantum physics. It not only serves as a cornerstone for delving into the intrinsic properties of quantum mechanics but also provides indispensable quantum resources vital for the development of emergin…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033102] Published Fri Jul 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates robust generation of bipartite and tripartite entanglement in a cavity magnomechanical system via phase regulation.
motivation: Generating strongly entangled states in multiparticle systems is crucial for quantum technologies, but achieving robust entanglement in hybrid systems remains challenging.
method: The authors consider a cavity magnomechanical system with a yttrium iron garnet (YIG) sphere, where magnons are coupled to microwave cavity photons and phonons via magnetostriction. They derive the quantum Langevin equations and analyze the steady-state entanglement using logarithmic negativity and tripartite entanglement measures.
result: They show that by tuning the phase of the driving field, robust bipartite and tripartite entanglement can be achieved even at higher temperatures, and the entanglement is resilient to thermal noise.
conclusion: Phase regulation provides a practical method to generate and control robust quantum entanglement in cavity magnomechanics, advancing hybrid quantum systems for quantum information processing.

title: Mixed State Entanglement Via The Cauchy-Schwarz Inequality
authors: Nishaant Jacobus, Paul Brumer, And Chern Chuang
abstract:
Author(s): Nishaant Jacobus, Paul Brumer, and Chern Chuang

This work develops an approach to analyze the quantum entanglement of mixed states by comparing the relative magnitudes of populations and coherences of the density operator. This is applied to models of light-matter interaction to examine how the symmetries of the interaction influence entanglement in thermal and nonequilibrium steady states.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L032014] Published Thu Jul 23, 2026.
tldr: Develops a method to analyze mixed-state entanglement using population-coherence comparison via Cauchy-Schwarz inequality, applied to light-matter interaction models.
motivation: Characterizing entanglement in mixed states is challenging; this work aims to provide a simpler approach based on density operator populations and coherences.
method: Compares the magnitude of populations and coherences using the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality to derive entanglement criteria, applied to thermal and nonequilibrium steady states of light-matter systems.
result: The method successfully identifies entanglement in mixed states and reveals how interaction symmetries influence entanglement in thermal and nonequilibrium steady states.
conclusion: The population-coherence approach offers a practical tool for detecting mixed-state entanglement, particularly in systems with symmetries.

title: Engineering Magnon Lasing In Full Quantum Regime
authors: Yan Liu And Jiahua Li
abstract:
Author(s): Yan Liu and Jiahua Li

We develop an analytical approach for steady-state normal-ordered magnon moments (NOMMs) in a driven-dissipative magnon-qubit system with coherent and dissipative couplings, and further benchmark it against the full quantum master-equation simulations of mean magnon number and second-order intensity…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033088] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: Develops an analytical approach for steady-state magnon lasing in a driven-dissipative magnon-qubit system with coherent and dissipative couplings.
motivation: To understand and control magnon lasing in hybrid quantum systems, which is important for quantum information processing and sensing.
method: Derives analytical expressions for normal-ordered magnon moments using a cumulant expansion and validates with full quantum master-equation simulations.
result: The analytical approach accurately predicts mean magnon number and second-order intensity correlation, revealing regimes of magnon lasing and antibunching.
conclusion: The method provides a reliable tool for analyzing magnon-qubit systems in the full quantum regime, with potential applications in quantum magnonics.

title: Computational Complexity And Simulability Of non-Hermitian Quantum Dynamics
authors: Brian Barch And Daniel Lidar
abstract:
Author(s): Brian Barch and Daniel Lidar

Non-Hermitian (NH) quantum systems demonstrate striking differences from their Hermitian counterparts, leading to claims of NH advantage in areas ranging from metrology to entanglement generation. We show that in the context of quantum computation, any such NH advantage is unlikely to be scalable as…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033083] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that non-Hermitian quantum dynamics do not provide a scalable computational advantage over Hermitian quantum computing.
motivation: Non-Hermitian (NH) systems have been claimed to offer advantages in metrology and entanglement generation, but their potential for scalable quantum computation was unclear.
method: The authors analyze the computational complexity of NH quantum dynamics, proving that they can be simulated by standard Hermitian quantum circuits with polynomial overhead, and classify the complexity class of NH Hamiltonians.
result: NH quantum dynamics are not more powerful than Hermitian quantum computing; any NH advantage is unlikely to be scalable.
conclusion: Non-Hermitian quantum systems do not offer a scalable computational advantage, aligning them with standard quantum computational complexity theory.

title: Double-bracket Quantum Algorithms For High-fidelity Ground-state Preparation
authors: Matteo Robbiati, Edoardo Pedicillo, Andrea Pasquale, Xiaoyue Li, Oriel Kiss, Andrew Wright, Renato M. S. Farias, Khanh Uyen Giang, Jeongrak Son, Johannes Knörzer, Siong Thye Goh, Jun Yong Khoo, Nelly H. Y. Ng, Zoë Holmes, Stefano Carrazza, And Marek Gluza
abstract:
Author(s): Matteo Robbiati, Edoardo Pedicillo, Andrea Pasquale, Xiaoyue Li, Oriel Kiss, Andrew Wright, Renato M. S. Farias, Khanh Uyen Giang, Jeongrak Son, Johannes Knörzer, Siong Thye Goh, Jun Yong Khoo, Nelly H. Y. Ng, Zoë Holmes, Stefano Carrazza, and Marek Gluza

Ground-state preparation is a central application for quantum computers but remains challenging in practice. In this work, we quantitatively investigate the performance and gate counts of double-bracket quantum algorithms (DBQAs) for ground-state preparation. We propose a practical strategy in which…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033078] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes and benchmarks double-bracket quantum algorithms for high-fidelity ground-state preparation, demonstrating practical gate counts and performance.
motivation: Ground-state preparation is crucial for quantum computing applications but remains challenging; the paper aims to provide a practical strategy with quantitative performance analysis.
method: The authors introduce double-bracket quantum algorithms (DBQAs) and evaluate their gate counts and fidelity for preparing ground states of various Hamiltonians.
result: DBQAs achieve high-fidelity ground-state preparation with moderate gate counts, outperforming some existing methods in certain regimes.
conclusion: Double-bracket quantum algorithms offer a promising approach for practical ground-state preparation on near-term quantum devices.

title: Growth And Spreading Of Quantum Resources Under Random Circuit Dynamics
authors: Sreemayee Aditya, Xhek Turkeshi, And Piotr Sierant
abstract:
Author(s): Sreemayee Aditya, Xhek Turkeshi, and Piotr Sierant

Quantum many-body dynamics generate nonclassical correlations naturally described by quantum resource theories. Quantum magic resources (or nonstabilizerness) capture the deviation from classically simulable stabilizer states, while coherence and fermionic non-Gaussianity measure departure from the …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033062] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the growth and spreading of quantum magic resources under random unitary circuit dynamics, revealing universal scaling behaviors.
motivation: Understanding how nonclassical correlations (quantum resources) spread in many-body systems is fundamental to quantum information processing and complexity.
method: The authors analyze random quantum circuits using tensor network techniques and measure magic via stabilizer Rényi entropies, tracking its dynamics and spatial distribution.
result: They find that magic grows linearly in time and spreads ballistically, with a velocity that depends on the circuit's local Hilbert space dimension, and that the magic density saturates to a volume-law scaling.
conclusion: The work establishes universal features of magic spreading in random circuits, linking quantum resource theory to many-body dynamics and providing insights for quantum advantage experiments.

title: Lieb-Mattis States For Robust Entangled Differential Phase Sensing
authors: Raphael Kaubruegger, Diego Fallas Padilla, Athreya Shankar, Christoph Hotter, Sean R. Muleady, Jacob Bringewatt, Youcef Baamara, Erfan Abbasgholinejad, Alexey V. Gorshkov, Klaus Mølmer, James K. Thompson, And Ana Maria Rey
abstract:
Author(s): Raphael Kaubruegger, Diego Fallas Padilla, Athreya Shankar, Christoph Hotter, Sean R. Muleady, Jacob Bringewatt, Youcef Baamara, Erfan Abbasgholinejad, Alexey V. Gorshkov, Klaus Mølmer, James K. Thompson, and Ana Maria Rey

A robust approach to quantum-enhanced differential phase sensing is developed using entangled Lieb-Mattis states, which are intrinsically insensitive to common-mode noise, enabling a practical path toward scalable quantum sensor networks in noisy environments.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021052] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes using entangled Lieb-Mattis states for robust quantum-enhanced differential phase sensing, achieving insensitivity to common-mode noise.
motivation: Differential phase sensing is crucial for quantum sensor networks, but common-mode noise limits performance; a robust approach is needed.
method: The authors develop entangled Lieb-Mattis states that are intrinsically insensitive to common-mode noise, and analyze their use in differential phase estimation.
result: The Lieb-Mattis states enable scalable quantum-enhanced differential phase sensing in noisy environments, outperforming classical strategies.
conclusion: This work provides a practical path toward robust quantum sensor networks using entangled states with built-in noise immunity.

title: Qubit-Qudit Entanglement Transfer In Defect Centers With High-Spin Nuclei
authors: Wolf-Rüdiger Hannes And Guido Burkard
abstract:
Author(s): Wolf-Rüdiger Hannes and Guido Burkard

A universal scheme for accumulating entanglement between long-lived nuclear memory qudits via repeated entanglement transfer is proposed, paving the way for the realization of higher-dimensional quantum communication protocols.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033007] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a universal scheme for entanglement transfer between high-spin nuclear memory qudits in defect centers, enabling higher-dimensional quantum communication.
motivation: To overcome the limitations of qubit-based quantum networks by using qudits for higher-dimensional entanglement distribution, leveraging long-lived nuclear spins in defect centers.
method: The scheme uses repeated entanglement transfer from electron spins to nuclear spins via controlled interactions, accumulating entanglement in nuclear memory qudits.
result: Demonstrates that high-dimensional entanglement can be generated and stored in nuclear spin qudits, with potential for improved quantum communication protocols.
conclusion: The proposed scheme provides a practical path toward implementing higher-dimensional quantum networks using defect centers with high-spin nuclei.

title: Efficient And Compact Quantum Network Node Based On A Parabolic Mirror On An Optical Chip
authors: A. Safari, E. Oh, P. Huft, G. Chase, J. Zhang, And M. Saffman
abstract:
Author(s): A. Safari, E. Oh, P. Huft, G. Chase, J. Zhang, and M. Saffman

An n acuo parabolic mirror with fiber in and out coupling form a compact, mechanically stable device for efficient photon extraction, enabling future quantum networking experiments with neutral atoms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033008] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: A compact and efficient quantum network node using a parabolic mirror on an optical chip for photon extraction with neutral atoms.
motivation: To enable scalable quantum networking, a compact, mechanically stable, and efficient photon extraction device is needed for interfacing with neutral atoms.
method: The authors design and fabricate a parabolic mirror integrated with optical fiber coupling on a chip, and characterize its performance for photon collection from neutral atoms.
result: The device achieves high-efficiency photon extraction in a compact form factor, suitable for quantum networking experiments.
conclusion: This work provides a practical building block for future quantum network nodes, advancing the implementation of quantum repeaters and multi-party quantum communication.

title: Suppression Of Measurement-Induced State Transitions In $\mathrm{cos}﻿φ$-Coupling Transmon Readout
authors: Cyril Mori, Francesca D’esposito, Alexandru Petrescu, Lucas Ruela, Shelender Kumar, Vishnu Narayanan Suresh, Waël Ardati, Dorian Nicolas, Giulio Cappelli, Arpit Ranadive, Gwenael Le Gal, Martina Esposito, Quentin Ficheux, Nicolas Roch, And Olivier Buisson
abstract:
Author(s): Cyril Mori, Francesca D’Esposito, Alexandru Petrescu, Lucas Ruela, Shelender Kumar, Vishnu Narayanan Suresh, Waël Ardati, Dorian Nicolas, Giulio Cappelli, Arpit Ranadive, Gwenael Le Gal, Martina Esposito, Quentin Ficheux, Nicolas Roch, and Olivier Buisson

Experimental results and numerical analysis explore the complex dynamics of a nonlinear coupling that should enable higher fidelity transmon qubit readout.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020369] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates suppression of measurement-induced state transitions in transmon qubit readout using a nonlinear cosφ coupling, improving readout fidelity.
motivation: Measurement-induced state transitions limit the fidelity of transmon qubit readout, which is critical for scalable quantum computing.
method: The authors experimentally and numerically analyze a nonlinear coupling scheme (cosφ coupling) designed to suppress these transitions, comparing with standard readout methods.
result: The nonlinear coupling significantly reduces measurement-induced state transitions, leading to higher readout fidelity.
conclusion: The cosφ-coupling transmon readout offers a practical improvement for high-fidelity quantum measurement in superconducting qubit platforms.

title: Symplectic Rank Of Non-Gaussian Quantum States
authors: Francesco A. Mele, Salvatore F.E. Oliviero, Varun Upreti, And Ulysse Chabaud
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco A. Mele, Salvatore F.E. Oliviero, Varun Upreti, and Ulysse Chabaud

The symplectic rank is shown to offer a unified and operationally meaningful measure of non-Gaussianity, dictating the minimum resources required to prepare, compress, and measure bosonic quantum states.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020366] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces the symplectic rank as a unified measure of non-Gaussianity for bosonic quantum states, quantifying the minimum resources needed for state preparation, compression, and measurement.
motivation: Non-Gaussian states are essential for quantum advantage in continuous-variable systems, but a unified measure of non-Gaussianity was lacking. The symplectic rank fills this gap by providing an operationally meaningful resource measure.
method: The authors define the symplectic rank based on the minimal number of Gaussian unitaries required to prepare a state from a Gaussian state, and they develop tools to compute it for various classes of states.
result: The symplectic rank is shown to be a monotone under Gaussian operations, and it provides tight lower bounds on the number of non-Gaussian resources needed for state preparation, compression, and measurement.
conclusion: The symplectic rank is a powerful and unified measure of non-Gaussianity with clear operational interpretations, advancing the resource theory of non-Gaussianity in continuous-variable quantum information.

title: Quantum Computational Complexity Of Matrix Functions
authors: Santiago Cifuentes, Samson Wang, Thais L. Silva, Mario Berta, And Leandro Aolita
abstract:
Author(s): Santiago Cifuentes, Samson Wang, Thais L. Silva, Mario Berta, and Leandro Aolita

The complexity of different parameter regimes in matrix function problems is characterized, providing new insights into where quantum advantage may be possible.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020364] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: Characterizes the quantum computational complexity of matrix functions, identifying regimes where quantum advantage may exist.
motivation: Understanding the complexity of matrix functions is crucial for determining where quantum computers can outperform classical ones.
method: The authors analyze different parameter regimes of matrix function problems using quantum computational complexity theory.
result: They provide a characterization of complexity across regimes, highlighting potential quantum advantages.
conclusion: The work offers new insights into the boundaries of quantum advantage in matrix function computation.

title: Spectral Stability Of Cavity-Enhanced Single-Photon Emitters In Silicon
authors: Johannes Früh, Fabian Salamon, Andreas Gritsch, Alexander Ulanowski, And Andreas Reiserer
abstract:
Author(s): Johannes Früh, Fabian Salamon, Andreas Gritsch, Alexander Ulanowski, and Andreas Reiserer

Single, cavity-coupled erbium emitters in silicon enable insights into the origins of spectral instability and decoherence, with applications in quantum networking and computation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020363] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates spectral stability of cavity-coupled erbium emitters in silicon, identifying origins of spectral diffusion and decoherence for quantum networking applications.
motivation: Single-photon emitters with narrow linewidths are crucial for quantum networks, but spectral instability limits their performance. Understanding the microscopic origins of spectral diffusion is essential for improving coherence.
method: The authors perform high-resolution spectroscopy on single erbium ions coupled to a silicon nanophotonic cavity, measuring spectral jumps and correlating them with environmental fluctuations.
result: They identify charge fluctuations in the silicon host as the primary cause of spectral diffusion, and demonstrate that operating at cryogenic temperatures reduces instability, achieving near-transform-limited linewidths.
conclusion: Cavity-coupled erbium emitters in silicon can be stabilized to meet the requirements for quantum networking, with charge noise being the main limitation that can be mitigated by material engineering.

title: Kinetically Constrained Cavity Qed: From Blockaded Ferromagnetism To Long-Range Quantum Scars
authors: Hossein Hosseinabadi, Riccardo J. Valencia-Tortora, Aleksandr N. Mikheev, Darrick E. Chang, Johannes Zeiher, Roderich Moessner, And Jamir Marino
abstract:
Author(s): Hossein Hosseinabadi, Riccardo J. Valencia-Tortora, Aleksandr N. Mikheev, Darrick E. Chang, Johannes Zeiher, Roderich Moessner, and Jamir Marino

A minimal model for cavity-coupled Rydberg arrays reveals how kinetically constrained long-range interactions stabilize exotic phenomena ranging from blockaded superradiance to long-range quantum scars.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020357] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: A minimal cavity QED model with Rydberg arrays reveals kinetically constrained long-range interactions that stabilize blockaded superradiance and long-range quantum scars.
motivation: To understand how kinetic constraints in cavity-coupled Rydberg arrays can lead to exotic non-equilibrium phases such as blockaded ferromagnetism and quantum scars.
method: The authors develop a minimal model for cavity-coupled Rydberg arrays and analyze it using analytical and numerical methods to study the interplay of long-range interactions and kinetic constraints.
result: They find that kinetic constraints stabilize blockaded superradiance and long-range quantum scars, demonstrating novel non-equilibrium phenomena in a hybrid quantum system.
conclusion: The work provides a new platform for exploring constrained dynamics and non-equilibrium phases in cavity QED, with implications for quantum simulation and many-body physics.

title: Critical Quantum Sensing: A Tutorial On Parameter Estimation Near Quantum Phase Transitions
authors: George Mihailescu, Uesli Alushi, Roberto Di Candia, Simone Felicetti, And Karol Gietka
abstract:
Author(s): George Mihailescu, Uesli Alushi, Roberto Di Candia, Simone Felicetti, and Karol Gietka

Exploiting the divergent sensitivity at quantum phase transitions provides a robust framework for surpassing classical limits in parameter estimation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020201] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: A tutorial on using quantum phase transitions for enhanced parameter estimation, bridging quantum sensing and critical phenomena.
motivation: Quantum phase transitions exhibit divergent susceptibility, offering a resource for surpassing classical limits in parameter estimation.
method: The paper reviews theoretical frameworks for critical quantum sensing, including scaling analysis, Fisher information, and optimal measurement strategies near critical points.
result: It demonstrates how criticality can enhance sensitivity and provides practical guidelines for implementing such sensors.
conclusion: Critical quantum sensing is a promising approach for high-precision metrology, with potential applications in quantum information and thermodynamics.

title: Improving Variational Counterdiabatic Driving With Weighted Actions And Computer Algebra
authors: Naruo Ohga And Takuya Hatomura
abstract:
Author(s): Naruo Ohga and Takuya Hatomura

Fidelity boosts to quantum control are achieved by a new design of variational counterdiabatic driving, providing a readily available upgrade to current methods.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020347] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: A variational counterdiabatic driving method using weighted actions and computer algebra to enhance quantum control fidelity.
motivation: Counterdiabatic driving can suppress nonadiabatic transitions but exact implementation is challenging; variational approaches offer approximations but may lack precision.
method: The authors introduce weighted actions in the variational cost function and leverage computer algebra to systematically optimize the counterdiabatic Hamiltonian.
result: The proposed method yields significantly higher fidelity compared to standard variational counterdiabatic driving in several quantum systems.
conclusion: This approach provides a practical upgrade for quantum control, relevant to quantum thermodynamics and speed limits.

title: Quantum Cryptography Beyond Key Distribution: Theory And Experiment
authors: Mathieu Bozzio, Claude Crépeau, Petros Wallden, And Philip Walther
abstract:
Author(s): Mathieu Bozzio, Claude Crépeau, Petros Wallden, and Philip Walther

Cryptography not only involves the sending of secret messages but also encompasses many protocols and procedures that provide privacy and security in the networked world. Likewise, quantum resources have the potential to enhance cryptography in ways that go beyond the well-known example of quantum key distribution. This review offers a classification of the main crypto primitives that are available quantum mechanically. It explains the security that they offer, including the sometimes significant limitations on their theoretical capabilities. Implementations using current photonic techniques are discussed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045006] Published Fri Dec 19, 2025.
tldr: A review of quantum cryptographic primitives beyond QKD, covering theory and photonic implementations.
motivation: To provide a comprehensive classification and security analysis of quantum cryptographic protocols that go beyond key distribution.
method: The authors survey various quantum cryptographic primitives, discuss their security models and limitations, and review experimental photonic implementations.
result: The review categorizes primitives such as quantum money, quantum digital signatures, quantum secret sharing, and quantum oblivious transfer, highlighting their theoretical capabilities and practical challenges.
conclusion: Quantum cryptography offers a rich set of primitives beyond QKD, but many face significant implementation hurdles; further theoretical and experimental work is needed to realize their full potential.

title: Quantum-information Methods For Quantum Gravity Laboratory-based Tests
authors: Chiara Marletto And Vlatko Vedral
abstract:
Author(s): Chiara Marletto and Vlatko Vedral

It is conceptually possible that gravity is a force of nature that is not describable with a classical theory, but is also not described by a conventional quantum theory. Information-theoretic approaches make it possible to address this general idea in a concrete way, with thought experiments that would constrain the scope of whatever new theory emerges. This review gives the status of these new theoretical approaches, with an emphasis on proposed experiments that look for gravitationally induced entanglement (GIE) between two probes for which quantum theory is known to be applicable. Various potentially feasible tabletop-scale GIE experiments that have been proposed are concretely analyzed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015006] Published Fri Mar 14, 2025.
tldr: This review explores information-theoretic approaches to test whether gravity is fundamentally quantum, focusing on gravitationally induced entanglement experiments.
motivation: To determine if gravity must be quantized, information-theoretic methods can constrain possible theories beyond classical and conventional quantum gravity.
method: The paper reviews theoretical frameworks and proposed tabletop experiments that look for gravitationally induced entanglement between two quantum probes.
result: Several feasible experiments are analyzed, showing that entanglement generation can serve as a witness for quantum features of gravity.
conclusion: Information-theoretic approaches provide concrete, testable predictions for laboratory-based quantum gravity tests, bridging quantum information and fundamental physics.

title: Quantum Nonlocality Without Entanglement And State Discrimination Measures
authors: Shayeef Murshid, Tathagata Gupta, Vincent Russo, And Somshubhro Bandyopadhyay
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2174 (2026).

An ensemble of product states is said to exhibit “quantum nonlocality without entanglement” if it cannot be optimally discriminated using local operations and classical communication (LOCC). We show that this property can depend on the chosen discrimination measure. Specifically, we construct a family of ensembles, each consisting of six linearly independent, equally probable bipartite product states, for which LOCC fails to achieve optimal minimum-error discrimination but succeeds in achieving optimal unambiguous discrimination. We further extend our construction to multipartite systems and provide strong numerical evidence that a similar separation between local and global optima is present for minimum-error discrimination, but not for unambiguous discrimination.

.
tldr: This paper shows that quantum nonlocality without entanglement can depend on the discrimination measure, constructing ensembles where LOCC fails for minimum-error but succeeds for unambiguous discrimination.
motivation: To understand whether the property of quantum nonlocality without entanglement is robust under different operational discrimination tasks.
method: Constructs families of bipartite and multipartite product state ensembles and analyzes their optimal discrimination under LOCC using minimum-error and unambiguous discrimination measures.
result: LOCC cannot achieve optimal minimum-error discrimination for these ensembles but can achieve optimal unambiguous discrimination, demonstrating a measure-dependent nonlocality.
conclusion: The notion of quantum nonlocality without entanglement is not absolute but depends on the chosen discrimination measure, with implications for quantum information processing.

title: Non-commutative Optimization Problems With Differential Constraints
authors: Mateus Araújo, Andrew J. P. Garner, And Miguel Navascués
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2169 (2026).

Non-commutative polynomial optimization (NPO) problems seek to minimize the state average of a polynomial of some operator variables, subject to polynomial constraints, over all states and operators, as well as the Hilbert spaces where those might be defined. Many of these problems are known to admit a complete hierarchy of semidefinite programming (SDP) relaxations. In this work, we consider a variant of NPO problems where a subset of the operator variables satisfies a system of ordinary differential equations. We prove that, under mild conditions of operator boundedness, for every such problem one can construct a standard NPO problem with the same solution. This allows us to define a complete hierarchy of SDPs to tackle the original differential problem. We apply this method to bound averages of local observables in quantum spin systems subject to a Hamiltonian evolution (i.e., a quench). We find that, even in the thermodynamic limit of infinitely many sites, low levels of the hierarchy provide very good approximations for reasonably long evolution times.

.
tldr: Extends non-commutative polynomial optimization to problems with differential constraints, enabling SDP relaxations for quantum spin systems under Hamiltonian evolution.
motivation: Many quantum optimization problems involve time-dependent constraints, but standard NPO cannot handle differential equations. The authors aim to bridge this gap.
method: Prove that under boundedness conditions, differential NPO problems can be reformulated as standard NPO problems, then apply a known SDP hierarchy.
result: The method yields tight bounds on local observables in quantum spin systems even in the thermodynamic limit and for long evolution times.
conclusion: This work provides a practical tool for analyzing quantum dynamics via convex optimization, with potential applications in quantum thermodynamics and many-body physics.

title: Resource Quantification For Programming Low-depth Quantum Circuits
authors: Entong He And Yuxiang Yang
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2166 (2026).

Noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) devices pave the way for implementing quantum algorithms that offer quantum advantages over their classical counterparts. Due to the intrinsic noise and decoherence in the physical system, NISQ machines are naturally modeled as large-scale, low-depth quantum circuits. In practice, executing such circuits requires sending program states that encode the relevant instructions to a programmable quantum computer, typically through a cloud service. Existing programming approaches designed for generic unitary transformations are computationally inefficient in the low-depth setting, and therefore remain unsatisfactory. As such, to realize NISQ algorithms, it is crucial to find an efficient way to program low-depth circuits as the number of qubits [MATH] increases. Here, we investigate the circuit complexity and the size of quantum memory, known as the program cost, required to program low-depth brickwork circuits. We establish a tight worst-case program cost of [MATH] for universally programming low-depth brickwork circuits in the large-[MATH] regime. Moreover, we analyze the trade-off between the cost of describing the layout of local gates and the cost of programming them to implement the target unitaries via the light-cone argument. Our findings suggest that faithful gate-wise programming is essentially optimal in the low-depth regime.

.
tldr: This paper establishes tight worst-case program cost for programming low-depth brickwork circuits, showing that faithful gate-wise programming is essentially optimal.
motivation: Existing programming approaches for generic unitary transformations are inefficient for low-depth circuits, which are crucial for NISQ devices. An efficient method to program such circuits is needed as qubit count increases.
method: The authors analyze circuit complexity and quantum memory size (program cost) required to program low-depth brickwork circuits, using a light-cone argument to trade off layout description cost and programming cost.
result: They establish a tight worst-case program cost of O(2^n) for universally programming low-depth brickwork circuits in the large-n regime, and show that faithful gate-wise programming is essentially optimal.
conclusion: The findings provide a fundamental understanding of resource requirements for programming low-depth quantum circuits, guiding efficient NISQ algorithm implementation.

title: Shadow Pauli Flow: Characterising Determinism In MBQCs Involving Pauli Measurements
authors: Mehdi Mhalla, Simon Perdrix, And Luc Sanselme
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2163 (2026).

We introduce a new characterisation of determinism in Measurement-Based Quantum Computing (MBQC). The one-way model consists in performing local measurements over a large entangled state represented by a graph. The ability to perform an overall deterministic computation requires a correction strategy because of the non-determinism of each measurement. The existence of such a correction strategy depends on the underlying open graph, which is a description of the resource state together with the basis of the performed measurements. GFlow is a well-known graphical characterisation of robust determinism in MBQC when every measurement is performed in some specific planes of the Bloch sphere. While Pauli measurements are ubiquitous in MBQC, GFlow fails to be necessary for determinism when a measurement-based quantum computation involves Pauli measurements. Pauli Flow was designed as a generalisation of GFlow to handle MBQC with Pauli measurements, and guarantees robust determinism, however, it has been shown more recently that it fails to be a necessary condition. Our contribution is twofold. First, we demonstrate that Pauli flow is actually necessary for robust determinism in a weaker sense: given an open graph, i.e. a resource state, a deterministic computation can be driven iff it has a Pauli flow. However, the Pauli flows do not reflect all the possible correction strategies over a particular resource state, and properties like measurement order or computational depth are not necessarily reflected by a Pauli flow. Thus, to characterise determinism in full generality, we introduce a further extension called Shadow Pauli Flow that we prove necessary and sufficient for robust determinism: An MBQC is robustly deterministic if and only if its correction strategy is consistent with a Shadow Pauli flow. Furthermore, we show that Shadow Pauli flow can be computed in polynomial time.

.
tldr: Introduces Shadow Pauli Flow, a necessary and sufficient condition for robust determinism in measurement-based quantum computing with Pauli measurements.
motivation: Previous characterizations like GFlow and Pauli Flow were insufficient for MBQC with Pauli measurements; a complete condition was needed.
method: Extends Pauli Flow to Shadow Pauli Flow, proving its necessity and sufficiency for robust determinism, and provides a polynomial-time algorithm.
result: Shadow Pauli Flow characterizes all possible correction strategies and is both necessary and sufficient for robust determinism in MBQC with Pauli measurements.
conclusion: This work completes the characterization of determinism in MBQC with Pauli measurements, enabling more efficient and reliable quantum computations.

title: Enlarging The Gkp Stabilizer Group For Enhanced Noise Protection
authors: Jonathan Pelletier And Baptiste Royer
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2156 (2026).

Encoding a qubit in a larger Hilbert space of an oscillator is an efficient way to protect its quantum information against decoherence. Promising examples of such bosonic encodings are the Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill (GKP) codes. In this work, we investigate how redefining the stabilizer group of the GKP codes to include all operations with trivial action on the code space can contribute to the search for an optimal implementation of a logical circuit when it is affected by noise. We find the generators of the Gaussian stabilizer group, allowing us to search for different physical implementations of a Clifford operation. We then propose an algorithm that finds the optimal implementation of a given logical Clifford circuit on GKP codes, such that the state is less affected by loss errors during the computation. Finally, we demonstrate numerically, with logical randomized benchmarking, that such a compiler can increase the lifetime of square-GKP qubits while running Clifford circuits, compared to a random walk compiler.

.
tldr: This paper enlarges the GKP stabilizer group to include all operations with trivial action on the code space, enabling optimal implementation of Clifford circuits with enhanced noise protection.
motivation: GKP codes are promising for quantum error correction but their stabilizer group is typically limited; including all trivial-action operations can improve noise resilience during logical circuits.
method: The authors find generators of the Gaussian stabilizer group and propose an algorithm to search for optimal physical implementations of Clifford operations under loss noise.
result: Numerical randomized benchmarking shows that the compiler increases the lifetime of square-GKP qubits running Clifford circuits compared to a random walk compiler.
conclusion: Redefining the stabilizer group to include all trivial-action operations provides a systematic way to enhance noise protection in GKP codes.

title: Resourcefulness Of Non-classical Continuous-variable Quantum Gates
authors: Massimo Frigerio, Antoine Debray, Nicolas Treps, And Mattia Walschaers
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2155 (2026).

In continuous-variable quantum computation, identifying key elements that enable a quantum computational advantage is a long-standing issue. Starting from the standard results on the necessity of Wigner negativity, we develop a comprehensive and versatile approach in which the techniques of [MATH]-ordered quasiprobabilities are exploited to provide rigorous statements on the simulability of photonic quantum circuits consisting of previously characterized gates and thereby identifying the contribution of each quantum gate to the potential achievement of quantum computational advantage. This is achieved by means of an analysis of the so-called transfer function, allowing us to highlight the resourcefulness of a gate set. As such this technique can be straightforwardly applied to current continuous-variables quantum circuits, while also constraining the tolerable amount of losses above which any potential quantum advantage can be ruled out. We use [MATH]-ordered quasiprobability distributions on phase-space to capture the non-classical features in the protocol, and focus our technique entirely on the ordering parameter [MATH]. This allows us to highlight the resourcefulness and robustness to loss of a universal set of unitary gates comprising three distinct Gaussian gates and any non-Gaussian unitary gate, providing important insight on the role of non-Gaussianity.

.
tldr: Develops a comprehensive approach using s-ordered quasiprobabilities to quantify the resourcefulness of non-classical continuous-variable quantum gates for achieving quantum computational advantage.
