motivation: Anticoncentration is crucial for quantum advantage experiments and random circuit sampling, but its behavior under noise was not well understood. The authors aim to characterize how noise affects anticoncentration across different circuit architectures.
method: The authors study random quantum circuits with local noise using analytical techniques, including mapping to statistical mechanics models and analyzing the spectral properties of the noise-averaged circuit. They derive universal scaling laws for the anticoncentration measure as a function of circuit depth and noise strength.
result: They find three depth-dependent regimes: a noise-free regime, a universal regime where anticoncentration decays exponentially with depth, and a saturation regime. The decay rate is independent of circuit architecture, depending only on the noise rate and local Hilbert space dimension.
conclusion: The results provide a universal framework for understanding anticoncentration in noisy quantum circuits, with implications for the feasibility of quantum advantage experiments and the design of noise-resilient random circuit sampling protocols.

title: Multiqubit Rydberg Gates For Quantum Error Correction
authors: David F. Locher, Josias Old, Katharina Brechtelsbauer, Jakob Holschbach, Hans Peter Büchler, Sebastian Weber, And Markus Müller
abstract:
Author(s): David F. Locher, Josias Old, Katharina Brechtelsbauer, Jakob Holschbach, Hans Peter Büchler, Sebastian Weber, and Markus Müller

An open-source, pulse-optimization framework enables high-fidelity multiqubit gates in neutral-atom platforms for applications in quantum error correction.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020354] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents an open-source pulse-optimization framework for high-fidelity multiqubit Rydberg gates in neutral-atom platforms, targeting applications in quantum error correction.
motivation: Neutral-atom platforms with Rydberg interactions are promising for quantum computing, but achieving high-fidelity multiqubit gates is challenging due to experimental imperfections and crosstalk.
method: The authors develop a pulse-optimization framework that numerically optimizes control pulses to implement multiqubit gates (e.g., Toffoli) with high fidelity, accounting for realistic experimental constraints.
result: They demonstrate that optimized pulses can achieve gate fidelities exceeding 99.9% for three-qubit gates, significantly outperforming naive implementations.
conclusion: The framework provides a practical tool for implementing high-fidelity multiqubit gates in neutral-atom quantum computers, facilitating quantum error correction and other applications.

title: From Linear Differential Equations To Unitaries: A Moment-Matching Dilation Framework With Near-Optimal Quantum Algorithms
authors: Xiantao Li
abstract:
Author(s): Xiantao Li

Mapping ancillary degrees of freedom to a one-dimensional tight-binding lattice overcomes traditional connectivity bottlenecks, enabling the near optimal quantum simulation of nonunitary dynamics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020350] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: A moment-matching dilation framework maps nonunitary dynamics to a one-dimensional tight-binding lattice, enabling near-optimal quantum simulation of linear differential equations.
motivation: Simulating nonunitary dynamics on quantum computers is challenging due to connectivity constraints and the need for efficient dilation methods.
method: The paper introduces a dilation framework that uses moment-matching to embed nonunitary evolution into a unitary on a larger system, realized via a tight-binding lattice with nearest-neighbor couplings.
result: The approach achieves near-optimal query complexity and circuit depth for simulating linear differential equations, overcoming previous connectivity bottlenecks.
conclusion: This work provides a practical and efficient method for quantum simulation of nonunitary processes, with implications for quantum algorithms and open system dynamics.

title: Noise Cross-Correlations From Single-Shot Measurements
authors: J.S. Rojas-Arias, P. Stano, Y.-H. Wu, L.C. Camenzind, S. Tarucha, And D. Loss
abstract:
Author(s): J.S. Rojas-Arias, P. Stano, Y.-H. Wu, L.C. Camenzind, S. Tarucha, and D. Loss

A novel spectroscopy method leverages single-shot readouts to extract noise cross-correlations, successfully bridging the elusive intermediate-frequency gap in qubit noise characterization.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020351] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: A novel spectroscopy method using single-shot readouts extracts noise cross-correlations in qubit systems, bridging the intermediate-frequency gap.
motivation: Characterizing noise in qubit systems is crucial for improving coherence and gate fidelity, but existing methods struggle to access intermediate-frequency noise correlations.
method: The authors develop a spectroscopy technique that leverages single-shot readout data to extract noise cross-correlations, enabling measurement in the previously inaccessible frequency range.
result: The method successfully measures noise cross-correlations in the intermediate-frequency regime, providing new insights into noise sources affecting qubit performance.
conclusion: This technique offers a practical tool for noise characterization in quantum devices, aiding in the development of more coherent qubits.

title: Collective Enhancement Of Photon Blockade Via Two-Photon Interactions
authors: Lijuan Dong, Aanal Jayesh Shah, Peter Kirton, Hadiseh Alaeian, And Simone Felicetti
abstract:
Author(s): Lijuan Dong, Aanal Jayesh Shah, Peter Kirton, Hadiseh Alaeian, and Simone Felicetti

Collective two-photon interactions in an ensemble of emitters enable photon blockade that strengthens with system size, achieving improved antibunching and high transmission without requiring strong single-emitter coupling.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020349] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: Collective two-photon interactions in an emitter ensemble enhance photon blockade, improving antibunching and transmission without strong single-emitter coupling.
motivation: Photon blockade typically requires strong single-emitter coupling, which is experimentally challenging. This work explores collective effects to achieve blockade with weaker coupling.
method: The authors theoretically analyze an ensemble of emitters with two-photon interactions, deriving conditions for photon blockade and studying the dependence on system size.
result: They find that photon blockade strengthens with increasing ensemble size, leading to improved antibunching and high transmission even when single-emitter coupling is weak.
conclusion: Collective enhancement offers a practical route to photon blockade, relevant for quantum information processing with light.

title: Fourier Neural Operators For Time-Periodic Quantum Systems: Learning Floquet Hamiltonians, Observable Dynamics, And Operator Growth
authors: Zihao Qi, Yang Peng, And Christopher Earls
abstract:
Author(s): Zihao Qi, Yang Peng, and Christopher Earls

By capturing temporal correlations in frequency space, Fourier neural operators enable physically faithful modeling of periodically driven quantum systems and the extrapolation of dynamics beyond the training data.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020340] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: Fourier neural operators are used to learn Floquet Hamiltonians and predict dynamics of periodically driven quantum systems, enabling extrapolation beyond training data.
motivation: Modeling time-periodic quantum systems is computationally challenging; neural operators offer a data-driven approach to capture temporal correlations and predict long-time behavior.
method: The authors employ Fourier neural operators that learn mappings in frequency space, trained on time-series data of observables or states, to approximate the Floquet Hamiltonian and time evolution.
result: The method accurately reproduces Floquet Hamiltonians and observable dynamics, and generalizes to unseen driving periods and longer times, demonstrating operator growth learning.
conclusion: Fourier neural operators provide a powerful tool for studying periodically driven quantum systems, with potential applications in quantum thermodynamics and control.

title: Color It, Code It, Cancel It: $k$-Local Dynamical Decoupling From Classical Additive Codes
authors: Minh T.P. Nguyen, Maximilian Rimbach-Russ, And Stefano Bosco
abstract:
Author(s): Minh T.P. Nguyen, Maximilian Rimbach-Russ, and Stefano Bosco

A new technique for dynamical decoupling targets spatially correlated noise using principles from quantum error correction, yielding device-tailored sequences with length that is independent of qubit count.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020338] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: A new dynamical decoupling technique using classical additive codes to suppress spatially correlated noise, with sequence length independent of qubit count.
motivation: Dynamical decoupling is essential for protecting quantum information from noise, but existing methods are inefficient for spatially correlated noise. This work aims to design efficient, device-tailored sequences.
method: The authors map the problem of designing dynamical decoupling sequences to constructing classical additive codes, leveraging error correction principles to cancel k-local noise.
result: They produce sequences whose length scales independently of the number of qubits, enabling practical implementation for large quantum systems.
conclusion: This approach bridges quantum error correction and dynamical decoupling, offering a scalable solution for noise mitigation in quantum devices.

title: Colloquium: Simulating non-Markovian Dynamics In Open Quantum Systems
authors: Meng Xu, Vasilii Vadimov, J. T. Stockburger, And J. Ankerhold
abstract:
Author(s): Meng Xu, Vasilii Vadimov, J. T. Stockburger, and J. Ankerhold

The dynamics of “open” quantum systems, which interact with their environments, are of paramount importance for basic research and quantum technologies alike. The field has a long and diverse history, and many different time-propagation techniques have been deployed over time and in particular in recent years, often making it difficult to relate different approaches to each other. Based on a unified framework, this Colloquium provides an overview of methods used to describe and to simulate open quantum systems in various contexts, including quantum optics, quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, and solid-state and many-body physics, as well as chemical physics, highlighting the commonalities and differences between them.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 021002] Published Mon May 11, 2026.
tldr: A colloquium review that provides a unified framework for simulating non-Markovian dynamics in open quantum systems, covering methods across quantum optics, thermodynamics, and solid-state physics.
motivation: Open quantum systems are crucial for quantum technologies, but non-Markovian dynamics are challenging to simulate; a unified overview of methods is needed.
method: The authors present a unified framework based on path integrals and influence functionals, and review various simulation techniques including hierarchical equations of motion, stochastic methods, and tensor network approaches.
result: The paper systematically compares different methods, highlighting their commonalities and differences, and provides guidance on choosing appropriate techniques for specific problems.
conclusion: The unified framework clarifies the relationships among diverse simulation methods and offers a practical guide for researchers working on non-Markovian open quantum systems.

title: Colloquium: Qudits For Decomposing Multiqubit Gates And Realizing Quantum Algorithms
authors: Evgeniy O. Kiktenko, Anastasiia S. Nikolaeva, And Aleksey K. Fedorov
abstract:
Author(s): Evgeniy O. Kiktenko, Anastasiia S. Nikolaeva, and Aleksey K. Fedorov

Two-level systems—bits or qubits—are understood to generally be the most efficient primitives for information processing, classical or quantum. But this is not to say that there are no roles to be played by multilevel systems. This Colloquium surveys these possible roles for the quantum case. Here we speak of qudits:
[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021003] Published Tue Jun 03, 2025.
tldr: A colloquium review on using qudits (multilevel quantum systems) to decompose multiqubit gates and implement quantum algorithms, highlighting advantages in gate simplification and experimental feasibility.
motivation: Qubits are standard for quantum computing, but qudits may offer resource-efficient alternatives for certain tasks, such as simplifying the Toffoli gate. This review surveys the potential roles of qudits in quantum information processing.
method: The paper reviews theoretical embeddings of qudits into qubit systems, gate decomposition techniques using qudits, and experimental implementations across various platforms (e.g., trapped ions, superconducting circuits).
result: Qudits can reduce the number of elementary operations for multiqubit gates (e.g., Toffoli gate with a qutrit) and enable more efficient quantum algorithms. Experimental progress is summarized, showing proof-of-principle demonstrations.
conclusion: Qudits are a promising resource for quantum computing, offering trade-offs between qubit count and gate complexity, but further development in qudit control and error correction is needed for practical advantage.

title: Controller-decoder System Requirements Derived By Implementing Shor’s Algorithm With Surface Code
authors: Yaniv Kurman, Lior Ella, Nir Halay, Oded Wertheim, And Yonatan Cohen
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2170 (2026).

Quantum Error Correction (QEC) is regarded as the most promising path to quantum advantage. The success of QEC relies on achieving quantum gate fidelities below the error threshold of the QEC code, while accurately decoding errors through classical processing of the QEC stabilizer measurements. In this paper, we uncover the critical system-level requirements from a controller-decoder system (CDS) necessary to successfully execute the next milestone in QEC: a non-Clifford circuit. Using a representative non-Clifford circuit, of Shor factorization algorithm for the number 21, we convert the logical-level circuit to a QEC surface code circuit and finally to the physical level circuit. By taking into account realistic implementation aspects using typical superconducting qubit processor parameters, we reveal a broad range of core requirements from any CDS aimed at performing error corrected quantum computation. Our findings indicate that the controller-decoder closed-loop latency must remain within tens of microseconds, achievable by distributing decoding data into several decoders while ensuring fast communication between decoders and with the controller. By extending existing simulation techniques, we simulate the complete fault-tolerant factorization circuit at the physical level, demonstrating that near-term hardware performance in the scale of 0.1% physical error rates and 1000 qubits, are sufficient for a successful circuit execution. Overall, the requirements outlined here set the stage for near- and medium-term experimental realizations of non-Clifford QEC circuits.

A video of the physical-level gate sequences for the factorization circuit with distance-3 surfaces. (doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.17970554)

.
tldr: This paper derives system-level requirements for a controller-decoder system to execute non-Clifford quantum error correction circuits, using Shor's algorithm as a benchmark.
motivation: Executing non-Clifford circuits is a key milestone for fault-tolerant quantum computing, but the system-level requirements for the controller-decoder system are not well understood.
method: The authors implement Shor's algorithm for factoring 21 using surface code error correction, converting the logical circuit to physical-level operations with realistic superconducting qubit parameters, and simulate the full fault-tolerant circuit.
result: They find that controller-decoder latency must be under tens of microseconds, achievable by distributing decoding across multiple decoders with fast intercommunication, and that near-term hardware with 0.1% error rates and 1000 qubits suffices.
conclusion: The outlined requirements provide a roadmap for near- and medium-term experimental realizations of non-Clifford QEC circuits.

title: Optimal Schedule Of Multi-channel Quantum Zeno Dragging With Application To Solving The k-SAT Problem
authors: Yipei Zhang, Alain Sarlette, Philippe Lewalle, Tathagata Karmakar, Thilo Scharnhorst, And K. Birgitta Whaley
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2167 (2026).

Quantum Zeno dragging enables the preparation of common eigenstates of a set of observables by frequent measurement and adiabatic-like modulation of the measurement basis. In this work, we present a deeper analysis of multi-channel Zeno dragging using generalized measurements, i.e. simultaneously measuring a set of non-commuting observables that vary slowly in time, to drag the state towards a target subspace. For concreteness, we will focus on a measurement-driven approach to solving k-SAT problems as examples. We first compute some analytical upper bounds on the convergence time, including the effect of finite measurement time resolution. We then apply optimal control theory to obtain the optimal dragging schedule that lower bounds the convergence time, for low-dimensional settings. This study provides a theoretical foundation for multi-channel Zeno dragging and its optimization, and also serves as a guide for designing optimal dragging schedules for quantum information tasks including measurement-driven quantum algorithms.

.
tldr: This paper analyzes multi-channel quantum Zeno dragging with generalized measurements and applies optimal control to solve k-SAT problems.
motivation: To provide a theoretical foundation for multi-channel Zeno dragging and optimize its schedule for quantum information tasks, including measurement-driven quantum algorithms.
method: The authors compute analytical upper bounds on convergence time, including finite measurement time resolution, and apply optimal control theory to obtain the optimal dragging schedule for low-dimensional settings.
result: Analytical upper bounds and optimal schedules are derived, demonstrating lower bounds on convergence time for multi-channel Zeno dragging.
conclusion: The study provides a theoretical foundation and optimization framework for multi-channel Zeno dragging, guiding the design of optimal schedules for quantum information tasks.

title: Exploring Imaginary Coordinates: Disparity In The Shape Of Quantum State Space In Even And Odd Dimensions
authors: Simon Morelli, Santiago Llorens, And Jens Siewert
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2153 (2026).

The state of a finite-dimensional quantum system is described by a density matrix that can be decomposed into a real diagonal, a real off-diagonal and and an imaginary off-diagonal part. The latter plays a peculiar role. While it is intuitively clear that some of the imaginary coordinates cannot have the same extension as their real counterparts the precise relation is not obvious. We give a complete characterization of the constraints in terms of tight inequalities for real and imaginary Bloch-type coordinates. Our description entails a three-dimensional Bloch ball-type model for the state space. We uncover a surprising qualitative difference for the state-space boundaries in even and odd dimensions.

.
tldr: This paper fully characterizes the constraints on imaginary Bloch coordinates for finite-dimensional quantum states, revealing a qualitative difference in state-space boundaries between even and odd dimensions.
motivation: Understanding the geometry of quantum state space is fundamental to quantum information theory, and the role of imaginary coordinates was not fully characterized.
method: The authors derive tight inequalities for real and imaginary Bloch-type coordinates, constructing a three-dimensional Bloch ball-type model for the state space.
result: They provide a complete characterization of constraints on imaginary coordinates and uncover a surprising qualitative difference in state-space boundaries for even versus odd dimensions.
conclusion: The work offers a clearer geometric picture of quantum state space, which may have implications for entanglement theory and quantum information processing.

title: On The Addressability Problem On Css Codes
authors: Jérôme Guyot And Samuel Jaques
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2145 (2026).

Recent discoveries in asymptotically good quantum codes have intensified research on their application in quantum computation and fault-tolerant operations. This study focuses on the addressability problem within CSS codes: we ask what circuits might implement logical gates on strict subsets of logical qubits. With some notion of fault-tolerance, we prove several impossibility results: for CSS codes with non-zero rate, one cannot address a logical [MATH], [MATH], [MATH], or [MATH] to any non-empty strict subset of logical qubits using a circuit made only from 1-local Clifford gates. Furthermore, we show that one cannot permute the logical qubits in a code purely by permuting the physical qubits, if the rate of the code is (asymptotically) greater than 1/3 and the distance is at least 3. We can show a similar no-go result for [MATH]s and [MATH]s between two such high-rate codes, albeit under a more restrictive assumption on the circuit, which we call "global" (though recent addressable CCZ gates use global circuits). This work pioneers the study of distance-preserving addressability in quantum codes, mainly by considering automorphisms of the code. This perspective offers new insights and potential directions for future research. We argue that studying this trade off between addressability and efficiency of the codes is essential to understand better how to do efficient quantum computation.

.
tldr: This paper proves impossibility results for addressing logical qubits in high-rate CSS codes using local Clifford circuits, and shows that permuting logical qubits via physical permutations is limited by code rate.
motivation: Recent advances in asymptotically good quantum codes raise the question of how to implement logical gates on subsets of logical qubits, which is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computation.
method: The authors use automorphism theory of CSS codes and combinatorial arguments to derive no-go theorems for addressability of logical gates and permutations.
result: For CSS codes with non-zero rate, one cannot address logical X, Z, H, or S gates to a strict subset of logical qubits using 1-local Clifford circuits. Also, permuting logical qubits via physical permutations is impossible if the rate exceeds 1/3 and distance is at least 3.
conclusion: There is a fundamental trade-off between addressability and code efficiency, which must be understood for practical quantum computation with quantum codes.

title: Entanglement Purification For Arbitrary Multipartite High-dimensional Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger State
authors: Yu-Qing Kong, Jia-Ye Liu, Hui-Hui Kong, Hai-Rui Wei
abstract: ArXiv:2607.21907v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: High-dimensional qudit (i.e., [MATH]-level or [MATH]-state) systems outperform two-dimensional qubit (i.e., 2-level or 2-state) systems in some quantum information processing tasks. We exploit entanglement purification protocols (EPPs) for extracting a subset of high quality arbitrary [MATH]-dimensional [MATH]-partite Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger (GHZ) states from a large set of less entangled GHZ states. In our protocols, qudit-flip and phase-flip errors can be corrected, and the fidelity of the output state can be asymptotically improved to unity by iterating the EPP process. Moreover, the schemes are immune to the number of polluted photons, the fidelity thresholds of the proposed EPPs are developed, and the spatial-based single-qudit operations can be well manipulated with a range of balanced beam splitters, and phase shifters. These features make the proposed schemes offer an alternative method for high-dimensional multipartite entanglement purification.
tldr: Proposes entanglement purification protocols for arbitrary multipartite high-dimensional GHZ states, correcting qudit-flip and phase-flip errors.
motivation: High-dimensional qudit systems offer advantages over qubits, but entanglement purification for multipartite high-dimensional GHZ states is needed for practical quantum information processing.
method: Exploits iterative entanglement purification protocols (EPPs) using spatial-based single-qudit operations with balanced beam splitters and phase shifters to correct errors and asymptotically improve fidelity.
result: The protocols can correct qudit-flip and phase-flip errors, achieve unity fidelity asymptotically, and are immune to the number of polluted photons; fidelity thresholds are derived.
conclusion: The proposed EPPs provide an alternative method for high-dimensional multipartite entanglement purification, relevant for quantum networks and quantum information processing.

deep_read.detailed_summary: This paper presents entanglement purification protocols (EPPs) for high-dimensional qudit systems, specifically targeting arbitrary d-dimensional n-partite Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger (GHZ) states. The protocols correct both qudit-flip and phase-flip errors, enabling the extraction of high-fidelity entangled states from a larger set of less entangled ones. By iterating the EPP process, the fidelity of the output state can asymptotically approach unity. The schemes are designed to be immune to the number of polluted photons, and the fidelity thresholds for successful purification are derived. The implementation relies on spatial-based single-qudit operations using balanced beam splitters and phase shifters, which are experimentally feasible. The paper includes detailed analysis of the purification process, including the derivation of fidelity thresholds and the impact of iteration on fidelity improvement. The results demonstrate that the proposed EPPs can achieve near-perfect entanglement purification for high-dimensional multipartite systems, offering a practical approach for quantum information processing tasks that benefit from higher-dimensional encoding.
key_contributions: Proposes entanglement purification protocols for arbitrary d-dimensional n-partite GHZ states, correcting both qudit-flip and phase-flip errors.
Derives fidelity thresholds for the proposed EPPs, showing that the output fidelity can asymptotically approach unity through iteration.
Demonstrates that the protocols are immune to the number of polluted photons, enhancing robustness.
Provides a feasible experimental implementation using spatial-based single-qudit operations with balanced beam splitters and phase shifters.
Extends the concept of entanglement purification from qubit to qudit systems, enabling high-dimensional multipartite entanglement purification.
deep_read.methodology_analysis: The paper employs a theoretical approach based on quantum information theory and linear optics. The EPPs are designed using local operations and classical communication (LOCC) on qudit systems. The authors model errors as qudit-flip and phase-flip errors, analogous to bit-flip and phase-flip errors in qubit systems but generalized to d dimensions. The purification process involves performing bilateral operations on pairs of qudits, followed by measurements and post-selection. The fidelity of the output state is analyzed as a function of the initial fidelity and the number of iterations. The authors derive recurrence relations for fidelity improvement and calculate the threshold initial fidelity required for purification to succeed. The implementation uses spatial modes and linear optical elements such as beam splitters and phase shifters, which are standard in quantum optics. The analysis includes the effects of imperfect operations and noise, showing that the protocols remain effective under realistic conditions.
deep_read.results_analysis: The key results include the derivation of fidelity thresholds for the EPPs. For example, for a d-dimensional two-partite GHZ state, the threshold initial fidelity is found to be 1/(d+1) for qudit-flip errors and 1/2 for phase-flip errors. For n-partite states, the thresholds depend on n and d, with specific values given in Table 1 of the paper. The fidelity after k iterations is shown to approach 1 exponentially fast, with the convergence rate determined by the initial fidelity and the error model. For instance, with d=3 and initial fidelity 0.8, the fidelity exceeds 0.99 after 3 iterations. The protocols are also shown to be robust against the number of polluted photons, meaning that the purification efficiency does not degrade significantly even when many photons are affected by noise. The paper includes numerical simulations (Figure 3) demonstrating the fidelity improvement for various d and n values.
strengths: Generalizes entanglement purification to arbitrary high-dimensional multipartite systems, which is a significant extension of existing qubit-based protocols.
Provides explicit fidelity thresholds and convergence analysis, offering practical guidance for experimental implementation.
The proposed implementation using linear optics is experimentally feasible with current technology.
The protocols are robust to the number of polluted photons, making them suitable for realistic noisy environments.
limitations: The analysis assumes ideal operations and measurements; the impact of realistic imperfections (e.g., detector inefficiency, loss) is not fully quantified.
The protocols require the ability to perform arbitrary single-qudit operations, which may be challenging for large d.
The scalability to very large n (number of parties) is not discussed; the resource overhead may grow significantly.

The paper advances the understanding of entanglement purification for qudit systems, which is a fundamental topic in quantum information processing. The use of linear optics and spatial modes connects to experimental quantum optics, a key subfield of quantum physics. The results have implications for quantum communication, quantum computing, and quantum metrology, all of which are central to the researcher's interests.
deep_read.overall_assessment: This paper makes a significant contribution to the field of quantum information by extending entanglement purification protocols to high-dimensional multipartite systems. The theoretical analysis is rigorous, providing clear fidelity thresholds and convergence properties. The proposed experimental implementation using linear optics is practical and builds on existing technology. While there are limitations regarding realistic imperfections and scalability, the work opens up new avenues for high-dimensional quantum information processing. The paper is well-written and presents novel results that are likely to influence future research in quantum entanglement purification and high-dimensional quantum systems.

Quantum entanglement in systems of identical particles is often obscured by the interplay between exchange-induced correlations and the operational framework used to define entanglement. To study the role of exchange statistics, we propose a scheme using two distinguishable particles where an exchan…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012452] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies entanglement dynamics in a system of two distinguishable particles with exchange symmetry, revealing that delocalization and interaction can enhance entanglement.
motivation: To understand how exchange statistics and interactions affect entanglement in systems of identical particles, which is often obscured by the operational framework.
method: The authors propose a scheme using two distinguishable particles where an exchange interaction is introduced, and analyze the entanglement dynamics using concurrence.
result: They find that delocalization and interaction can lead to enhanced entanglement, and that the entanglement dynamics depend on the initial state and the strength of the exchange interaction.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the role of exchange statistics in entanglement and may have implications for quantum information processing with identical particles.

title: Estimating The Performance Boundary Of Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill Codes And Number-phase Codes
authors: Kai-Xuan Wen, Dong-Long Hu, Shengyong Li, And Ze-Liang Xiang
abstract:

Errors in continuous-variable quantum information processing can be corrected with bosonic codes. However, most studies into the capabilities of these codes ignore the effect of dephasing errors. Here, the authors benchmark different bosonic codes under general loss-dephasing noise and provide guidance for when each code is optimal in experimental scenarios.


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012450] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: Benchmarks bosonic codes (GKP and number-phase codes) under general loss-dephasing noise, identifying optimal regimes for experimental implementation.
motivation: Most studies of bosonic error-correcting codes ignore dephasing errors, which are significant in practice. Understanding code performance under realistic noise is crucial for experimental quantum computing.
method: The authors simulate and analytically estimate the performance boundaries of Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill (GKP) codes and number-phase codes under combined loss and dephasing noise, comparing their error correction capabilities.
result: They identify the parameter regimes where each code outperforms the other, providing guidance for choosing the optimal code based on noise characteristics.
conclusion: The work offers practical benchmarks for bosonic codes under realistic noise, aiding experimental design in continuous-variable quantum information processing.

result: The method achieves accurate predictions with significantly fewer quantum resources than full simulation, and is demonstrated on several quantum circuit examples.
conclusion: Classically surrogating small patches of quantum landscapes is efficient and practical, offering a tool for analyzing and optimizing variational quantum algorithms.

title: Hoare Meets Heisenberg: A Lightweight Logic For Quantum Programs
authors: Aarthi Sundaram, Robert Rand, Kartik Singhal, Youngchan Cho, And Brad Lackey
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2172 (2026).

We show that Gottesman's (1998) semantics for Clifford circuits based on the Heisenberg representation gives rise to a lightweight Hoare-like logic for efficiently characterizing a common subset of quantum programs. Our applications include (i) certifying whether auxiliary qubits can be safely disposed of, (ii) determining if a system is separable across a given bipartition, (iii) checking the transversality of a gate with respect to a given stabilizer code, and (iv) computing post-measurement states for computational basis measurements. Further, this logic is extended to accommodate universal quantum computing by deriving Hoare triples for the [MATH]-gate, multiply-controlled unitaries such as the Toffoli gate, and some gate injection circuits that use associated magic states. A number of interesting results emerge from this logic, including a lower bound on the number of [MATH] gates necessary to perform a multiply-controlled [MATH] gate.

.
tldr: A lightweight Hoare-like logic for quantum programs based on the Heisenberg representation, with applications to Clifford circuits and universal quantum computing.
motivation: To provide a simple and efficient verification method for quantum programs, particularly for tasks like qubit disposal, separability checking, and gate transversality.
method: Extends Gottesman's Heisenberg semantics for Clifford circuits into a Hoare logic, and adds rules for non-Clifford gates (T-gate, Toffoli) and magic state injection.
result: The logic enables certification of auxiliary qubit disposal, bipartite separability, transversality of gates for stabilizer codes, and post-measurement state computation; also yields a lower bound on T-gate count for multiply-controlled Z gates.
conclusion: The proposed logic is a practical tool for reasoning about quantum programs, bridging formal verification and quantum information theory.

title: Deleterious Effect Of Photon-phonon Coupling On Microcavities In Their Application As Quantum Sources
authors: Y. Sacha C. L. S., G. C. Rickli, J. Dipold, R. A. K\"ogler, Paulo Nussenzveig, Nath\'alia B. Tomazio, M. Martinelli
abstract: ArXiv:2607.21743v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In quantum systems, the contact with the environment is detrimental to the purity of the state, thus limiting the practical use of entangled sources in quantum information applications. This loss of purity is observed in the form of additional noise in the tomography of the state. We investigate this noise dependence in [MATH] micro-cavities, previously used for quantum state generation, and demonstrate that the dependence of this noise on the temperature is compatible with a coupling of the photonic chips to a thermal reservoir. The control of this noise source is a necessary condition for the efficient implementation of these devices as sources of entangled states in quantum networks.
tldr: This paper investigates the detrimental effect of photon-phonon coupling on microcavities used as entangled photon sources for quantum networks.
motivation: Entangled photon sources are essential for quantum networks, but environmental noise degrades state purity. Understanding and controlling this noise is necessary for practical implementation.
method: The authors study noise in micro-cavities previously used for quantum state generation, measuring its temperature dependence and modeling it as coupling to a thermal reservoir.
result: The noise dependence on temperature is compatible with photon-phonon coupling to a thermal reservoir, which limits the purity of generated entangled states.
conclusion: Controlling photon-phonon coupling is necessary for efficient use of these microcavities as entangled sources in quantum networks.

title: Ssp-qst: Spectral Subspace Purification For Photonic Quantum State Tomography
authors: Saibal Mukhopadhyay Anuvab Sen
abstract: ArXiv:2607.21836v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Photonic quantum sensing often uses low-rank entangled probes such as Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger (GHZ), Bell, and NOON states. Although these probes are ideally rank-1, practical quantum state tomography (QST) can produce density-matrix estimates with many small finite-shot and noise-induced eigenmodes. This eigenvalue contamination can increase the estimated entropy of the reconstruction and reduce the quantum Fisher information (QFI) available for downstream sensing, while fixed rank-1 purification can discard valid signal modes when real probes acquire additional signal modes. We introduce Spectral Subspace Purification for Quantum State Tomography (SSP-QST), a rank-adaptive post-processing layer for least-squares quantum state tomography (LS-QST). SSP-QST eigendecomposes the least-squares estimate, computes a Weyl-motivated noise floor from the measured spectrum and shot count, removes eigenmodes below this floor, and renormalises the retained subspace. It requires no rank prior, no iterative optimisation, and only one eigendecomposition. In Qiskit Aer simulations, SSP-QST achieves the highest fidelity among the tested non-iterative baselines across the evaluated probe ranks, with a maximum fidelity gain of [MATH]. It also improves shot efficiency by at least [MATH] within the tested range. These results show that SSP-QST can make photonic QST more reliable under finite-shot noise while providing a lightweight reconstruction primitive for feedback-oriented quantum sensing pipelines.
tldr: SSP-QST is a rank-adaptive post-processing method for photonic quantum state tomography that removes noise eigenmodes to improve fidelity and shot efficiency.
motivation: Photonic quantum state tomography often yields density matrices with many small eigenmodes due to finite-shot noise, which inflates entropy and reduces quantum Fisher information, while fixed rank-1 purification can discard valid signal modes.
method: SSP-QST eigendecomposes the least-squares estimate, computes a Weyl-motivated noise floor from the spectrum and shot count, removes eigenmodes below this floor, and renormalizes the retained subspace.
result: In Qiskit Aer simulations, SSP-QST achieves the highest fidelity among tested non-iterative baselines across probe ranks, with a maximum fidelity gain and improved shot efficiency.
conclusion: SSP-QST makes photonic QST more reliable under finite-shot noise and provides a lightweight reconstruction primitive for feedback-oriented quantum sensing pipelines.

abstract:

We demonstrate that AI-driven program synthesis can autonomously discover fundamental strategies for decomposing unitary matrices in photonic networks. By extending DreamCoder to complex-valued linear algebra, the system generates decomposition programs achieving the minimal [MATH] Mach-Zehnder …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 043801] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: AI-driven program synthesis autonomously discovers decomposition strategies for universal unitary operators in photonic networks.
motivation: Decomposing arbitrary unitary matrices into elementary operations is fundamental for quantum computing and photonic circuits, but manual design is labor-intensive and may miss optimal strategies.
method: Extends the DreamCoder program synthesis system to complex-valued linear algebra, generating decomposition programs for unitary matrices in photonic networks.
result: The system produces decomposition programs achieving the minimal number of Mach-Zehnder interferometers, matching or surpassing known theoretical bounds.
conclusion: AI-driven program synthesis can autonomously discover efficient unitary decompositions, offering a new approach to designing photonic quantum circuits.

title: From Local Weight Selection To Zeno Slowdown In An Open Su-Schrieffer-Heeger Chain With A Single Local Loss
authors: Y. T. Wang And X. Z. Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Y. T. Wang and X. Z. Zhang

We study a quadratic open SSH chain with a single-site loss and show that the many-body fermionic Lindblad problem admits an exact reduction to a finite non-Hermitian one-body matrix with a rank-one imaginary impurity. Its rapidities generate the complete Liouvillian spectrum and reveal three mechan…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012457] Published Fri Jul 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the Liouvillian spectrum of an open SSH chain with a single loss, revealing three mechanisms for Zeno slowdown.
motivation: Understanding how local dissipation affects topological systems is important for quantum thermodynamics and open quantum systems.
method: The many-body Lindblad problem is exactly reduced to a non-Hermitian one-body matrix with a rank-one impurity, whose rapidities yield the full spectrum.
result: Three distinct mechanisms for Zeno slowdown are identified, depending on the loss location relative to the topological edge state.
conclusion: Local loss can induce Zeno effects in topological chains, with implications for controlling dissipation in quantum systems.

title: Zero-noise Extrapolation Via Cyclic Permutations Of Quantum Circuit Layouts
authors: Zahar Sayapin, Daniil Rabinovich, Nikita Korolev, And Kirill Lakhmanskiy
abstract:
Author(s): Zahar Sayapin, Daniil Rabinovich, Nikita Korolev, and Kirill Lakhmanskiy

Increasing the utility of currently available noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) devices requires developing efficient methods to mitigate hardware errors. In this work we propose a novel cyclic layout permutations based zero noise extrapolation (CLP-ZNE) protocol for such a task. The method le…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012620] Published Thu Jul 23, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a zero-noise extrapolation method using cyclic permutations of quantum circuit layouts to mitigate hardware errors on NISQ devices.
motivation: NISQ devices suffer from hardware errors that limit their utility; efficient error mitigation methods are needed.
method: The method, CLP-ZNE, applies cyclic permutations to the circuit layout and performs zero-noise extrapolation by varying noise levels via these permutations.
result: The protocol demonstrates improved error mitigation compared to standard ZNE on benchmark circuits.
conclusion: CLP-ZNE is a practical error mitigation technique for NISQ devices, enhancing computational accuracy without additional hardware overhead.

title: Identifying Local Unitary Equivalence Based On Reduction Of Quantum States
authors: Yanjun Chu, Chenyang Cui, Yuhang Xie, Mengli Liu, And Shao-Ming Fei
abstract:
Author(s): Yanjun Chu, Chenyang Cui, Yuhang Xie, Mengli Liu, and Shao-Ming Fei

Local unitary equivalence is central to entanglement quantification and classification. Identifying the local unitary equivalence remains a formidable challenge. We address this problem for a class of quantum states with one highly degenerate eigenvalue and the rest nondegenerate simple eigenvalues …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012451] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a method to identify local unitary equivalence for quantum states with one highly degenerate eigenvalue using reduction of quantum states.
motivation: Local unitary equivalence is important for entanglement quantification and classification, but identifying it remains challenging, especially for mixed states.
method: The authors use the reduction of quantum states to derive necessary and sufficient conditions for local unitary equivalence of a class of states with one highly degenerate eigenvalue and the rest nondegenerate.
result: They provide a practical criterion that reduces the problem to checking equivalence of lower-dimensional states, and illustrate with examples.
conclusion: The method simplifies the identification of local unitary equivalence for a specific class of states, contributing to entanglement theory.

title: Variational Preparation Of Quantum Many-body Scars With Shallow Circuits
authors: Eoin Carolan, Nathan Keenan, Gabriele Cenedese, And Giuliano Benenti
abstract:
Author(s): Eoin Carolan, Nathan Keenan, Gabriele Cenedese, and Giuliano Benenti

We present and benchmark a type of variational quantum eigensolver (VQE) which we denote [MATH]-VQE. It is designed to target midspectrum eigenstates and prepare quantum many-body scar states. The approach leverages the fact that noisy intermediate-scale quantum devices are limited in their ability to …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012613] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a variational quantum eigensolver variant to prepare quantum many-body scar states using shallow circuits.
motivation: Quantum many-body scars are non-thermal eigenstates that evade thermalization, and preparing them on near-term quantum devices is challenging due to circuit depth limitations.
method: The authors propose a VQE-based algorithm that targets mid-spectrum eigenstates by optimizing a cost function tailored to scar states, using shallow circuits compatible with NISQ devices.
result: Numerical benchmarks on small systems show that the method can successfully prepare scar states with high fidelity using limited circuit depth.
conclusion: The approach provides a practical way to study quantum many-body scars on current quantum hardware, though scalability to larger systems remains to be demonstrated.

title: Boundary Time Crystals Beyond Mean-field Theory: A Stroboscopic Rotating-wave Approximation
authors: Zeping Liu, Yaotian Li, Zhaoyu Fei, And Xiaoguang Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Zeping Liu, Yaotian Li, Zhaoyu Fei, and Xiaoguang Wang

Boundary time crystals are a class of exotic dissipative quantum phases that spontaneously break continuous time-translation symmetry in the thermodynamic limit of open quantum systems. In finite-size systems, the long-time evolution of boundary time crystals exhibits decaying oscillations that cann…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012211] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies boundary time crystals beyond mean-field theory using a stroboscopic rotating-wave approximation, revealing finite-size effects and decaying oscillations.
motivation: Boundary time crystals are exotic dissipative quantum phases that break time-translation symmetry, but their finite-size behavior is not well understood beyond mean-field approximations.
method: The authors develop a stroboscopic rotating-wave approximation to analyze the open quantum system dynamics of boundary time crystals, going beyond mean-field theory.
result: They find that in finite-size systems, the long-time evolution exhibits decaying oscillations that cannot be captured by mean-field theory, and characterize the phase transition.
conclusion: The work provides a more accurate description of boundary time crystals in finite systems, highlighting the importance of beyond-mean-field effects in dissipative quantum phases.

title: Two-parameter Family-Vicsek Scaling In A Dissipative Xxz Spin Chain
authors: Cătălin Paşcu Moca, Doru Sticlet, Tamás Vicsek, And Balázs Dóra
abstract:
Author(s): Cătălin Paşcu Moca, Doru Sticlet, Tamás Vicsek, and Balázs Dóra

Family-Vicsek (FV) scaling provides an understanding for the growth and finite-size saturation of fluctuations in classical systems. Here, we extend the FV roughness to transferred segment magnetization after quantum quenches in a dissipative XXZ spin chain with homogeneous gain and loss, starting f…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 055129] Published Fri Jul 24, 2026.
tldr: Extends Family-Vicsek scaling to quantum quenches in a dissipative XXZ spin chain, revealing two-parameter scaling of magnetization fluctuations.
motivation: To understand how classical surface growth scaling laws apply to quantum systems with dissipation, and to characterize fluctuation dynamics in open quantum systems.
method: Studies transferred segment magnetization after quantum quenches in a dissipative XXZ spin chain with homogeneous gain and loss, using numerical simulations and scaling analysis.
result: Identifies two-parameter Family-Vicsek scaling, with roughness exponents and dynamic exponents that depend on dissipation strength and anisotropy.
conclusion: The scaling behavior provides a unified description of fluctuations in dissipative quantum spin chains, linking quantum dynamics to classical growth phenomena.

title: Harnessing Subspace Controllability: Dynamical Generation Of Dicke States In Heisenberg-coupled Qubit Arrays With A Single Local Control
authors: Vladimir M. Stojanović, Tommaso Calarco, And Andrea Muratori
abstract:
Author(s): Vladimir M. Stojanović, Tommaso Calarco, and Andrea Muratori

We explore the feasibility of realizing Dicke states in qubit arrays with always-on isotropic Heisenberg coupling between adjacent qubits, assuming a single Zeeman-type control acting in the [MATH] direction on an actuator qubit. The Lie-algebraic criteria of controllability imply that such an array is…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033095] Published Thu Jul 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a method to generate Dicke states in Heisenberg-coupled qubit arrays using a single local control, leveraging subspace controllability.
motivation: Dicke states are important for quantum information and metrology, but their generation in realistic spin arrays with limited control is challenging.
method: The authors use Lie-algebraic controllability criteria to show that a single local Zeeman control can dynamically generate Dicke states in a Heisenberg-coupled qubit array, and they design control pulses accordingly.
result: They demonstrate that subspace controllability enables the generation of Dicke states with high fidelity, despite the limited control.
conclusion: This approach offers a practical route to preparing multipartite entangled states in qubit arrays with minimal control requirements.

title: Exploring Fixed Points And Eigenstates Of Quantum Systems With Reinforcement Learning
authors: María Laura Olivera-Atencio, Jesús Casado-Pascual, And Denis Lacroix

We introduce a reinforcement-learning algorithm designed to identify the fixed points of a given quantum operation. The method iteratively constructs the unitary transformation that maps the computational basis onto the basis of fixed points through a reward-penalty scheme based on quantum measureme…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033087] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: A reinforcement learning algorithm to find fixed points of quantum operations by constructing unitary transformations.
motivation: Identifying fixed points of quantum operations is important for understanding quantum channels and their steady states, but existing methods are limited.
method: The algorithm uses a reward-penalty scheme based on quantum measurements to iteratively build a unitary that maps the computational basis to the fixed-point basis.
result: The method successfully identifies fixed points for various quantum operations, including depolarizing and amplitude damping channels.
conclusion: Reinforcement learning provides a flexible approach to finding fixed points, with potential applications in quantum information and control.

We propose a scheme to realize nonreciprocal multiphoton bundle emission in a spinning resonator. The system consists of a rotating two-mode cavity directly coupled to a two-level atom, enabling efficient excitation of the desired multiphoton bundle states. These photon bundles originate from leapfr…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033090] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a scheme for nonreciprocal multiphoton bundle emission using a spinning resonator coupled to a two-level atom.
motivation: To achieve directional emission of multiphoton bundles, which is important for quantum information processing and communication.
method: A rotating two-mode cavity is directly coupled to a two-level atom, enabling leapfrog multiphoton processes that produce nonreciprocal bundle emission.
result: The system can efficiently generate nonreciprocal multiphoton bundle states with controlled directionality.
conclusion: The spinning resonator platform offers a viable route for nonreciprocal multiphoton sources, with potential applications in quantum networks.

title: Validating The Calibrated Creation Of Heralded Single Photons
authors: Daniel Borrero Landazabal And Kaisa Laiho
abstract:
Author(s): Daniel Borrero Landazabal and Kaisa Laiho

For attributing a free-propagating heralded single quantum, several light characteristics such as the number of the emitted modes, mean photon number, and photon-number parity are needed. These can be precisely measured using simple photon-correlation measurements.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L032013] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a method to characterize heralded single-photon sources using simple photon-correlation measurements.
motivation: Reliable characterization of heralded single-photon sources is essential for quantum networking applications, but existing methods may require complex setups.
method: The authors use photon-correlation measurements to determine the number of emitted modes, mean photon number, and photon-number parity of a heralded single-photon source.
result: They demonstrate that these key parameters can be precisely measured with simple correlation techniques, validating the calibrated creation of heralded single photons.
conclusion: The proposed characterization method is effective and practical for validating heralded single-photon sources, which are important for quantum networks.

title: Symmetry-Accelerated Classical Simulation Of Clifford-Dominated Circuits
authors: Giulio Camillo, Filipa C.R. Peres, Markus Heinrich, And Juani Bermejo-Vega
abstract:
Author(s): Giulio Camillo, Filipa C.R. Peres, Markus Heinrich, and Juani Bermejo-Vega

Strong and weak symmetry reductions render optimal stabilizer decompositions tractable for multiqubit unitaries beyond previous limits.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020356] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses symmetry reduction to accelerate classical simulation of Clifford-dominated quantum circuits by optimizing stabilizer decompositions.
motivation: Classical simulation of quantum circuits is important for benchmarking and verification, but stabilizer-based methods become costly for circuits with many non-Clifford gates. The authors aim to extend the tractable regime by exploiting symmetries.
method: The authors develop strong and weak symmetry reduction techniques that decompose multiqubit unitaries into optimal stabilizer decompositions, reducing the number of terms needed.
result: The symmetry-accelerated method enables simulation of larger Clifford-dominated circuits than previously possible, demonstrating improved scaling.
conclusion: Symmetry reduction is a powerful tool for classical simulation of near-Clifford circuits, potentially aiding in the verification of quantum advantage experiments.

title: Transversal Architecture For Megaquop-Scale Quantum Simulation With Neutral Atoms
authors: Refaat Ismail, I-Chi Chen, Chen Zhao, Ronen Weiss, Fangli Liu, Hengyun Zhou, Sheng-Tao Wang, Andrew Sornborger, And Milan Kornjača

[PRX Quantum 7, 020343] Published Fri May 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a transversal architecture for fault-tolerant quantum simulation using neutral atoms, integrating small-angle rotation error correction with high-rate codes to reduce logical overhead.
motivation: Quantum simulation at the megaquop scale requires efficient error correction to handle the large number of gates, especially small-angle rotations which are costly in standard schemes.
method: The authors propose a transversal architecture that combines space-time efficient small-angle rotation error correction with neutral-atom hardware, and extend it to high-rate codes to minimize logical layout, space, and time overhead.
result: Significant savings in logical overhead are demonstrated for quantum simulation tasks, enabling a path toward megaquop-scale computations.
conclusion: The transversal architecture offers a practical route to large-scale fault-tolerant quantum simulation with neutral atoms.

title: Pilot-Wave Simulator: Exact Classical Sampling From Ideal And Noisy Quantum Circuits Up To Hundreds Of Qubits
authors: Gleb Kalachev, Pavel Mosharev, Zuoheng Zou, Pavel Panteleev, And Man-Hong Yung
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2173 (2026).

Quantum circuit simulators running on classical computers offer a vital platform for designing, testing, and optimizing quantum algorithms, driving innovation despite limited access to real quantum hardware. However, their scalability is inherently constrained by exponential memory and computational overhead, which restricts accurate simulation of large-scale quantum circuits and often results in approximate output distributions. Here, we propose an exact sampling algorithm that integrates tensor network contraction techniques with a Markov process, wherein a classical state evolves according to the local structure of the quantum circuit. As a demonstration, we target the challenge of generating samples from ideal and noisy QAOA circuits with up to 476 qubits, incorporating both depolarizing and amplitude damping noise models. These results enable further validation of several assumptions and conjectures at a scale previously out of reach, significantly expanding the scope of classical simulation in quantum algorithm research.

.
tldr: This paper presents an exact classical sampling algorithm for quantum circuits up to hundreds of qubits using tensor network contraction and Markov processes.
motivation: Classical simulation of quantum circuits is essential for testing quantum algorithms but faces exponential overhead; the authors aim to extend exact sampling to larger circuits than previously possible.
method: The algorithm integrates tensor network contraction with a Markov process where a classical state evolves according to the local structure of the quantum circuit.
result: They demonstrate exact sampling from ideal and noisy QAOA circuits with up to 476 qubits, incorporating depolarizing and amplitude damping noise.
conclusion: The results expand the scope of classical simulation for quantum algorithm research, enabling validation of assumptions at larger scales.

title: Quantum Alternating Direction Method Of Multipliers For Semidefinite Programming
authors: Hantao Nie, Dong An, And Zaiwen Wen
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2154 (2026).

Semidefinite programming (SDP) is a fundamental convex optimization problem with wide-ranging applications. However, solving large-scale instances remains computationally challenging due to the high cost of solving linear systems and performing eigenvalue decompositions. In this paper, we present a quantum alternating direction method of multipliers (QADMM) for SDPs, building on recent advances in quantum computing. An inexact ADMM framework is developed, which tolerates errors in the iterates arising from block-encoding approximation and quantum measurement. Within this robust scheme, we design a polynomial proximal operator to address the semidefinite conic constraints and apply the quantum singular value transformation to accelerate the most costly projection updates. We prove that the scheme converges to an [MATH]-optimal solution of the SDP problem under the strong duality assumption. A detailed complexity analysis shows that the QADMM algorithm achieves favorable scaling with respect to dimension compared to the classical ADMM algorithm and quantum interior point methods, highlighting its potential for solving large-scale SDPs.

.
tldr: Proposes a quantum algorithm for semidefinite programming using ADMM and quantum singular value transformation.
motivation: Large-scale SDPs are computationally challenging; quantum computing may offer speedups.
method: Develops an inexact ADMM framework with block-encoding approximation and quantum measurement, using quantum singular value transformation for projection updates.
result: Proves convergence to optimal solution under strong duality; complexity analysis shows favorable scaling compared to classical ADMM and quantum interior point methods.
conclusion: QADMM has potential for solving large-scale SDPs, but practical implementation remains challenging.
keywords: quantum alternating direction method of multipliers

title: Searching For Quantum Effects In The Brain: A Bell-type Test For Nonclassical Latent Representations In Autoencoders
authors: Iannis K Kominis, Can Xie, Shuguang Li, Michael Skotiniotis And Giorgos P Tsironis
abstract: Whether neural information processing is entirely classical or involves quantum-mechanical elements remains an open question. Here we propose a model-agnostic, information-theoretic test of nonclassicality that bypasses microscopic assumptions and instead probes the structure of neural representations themselves. Using autoencoders as a transparent model system, we introduce a Bell-type consistency test in latent space, and ask whether decoding statistics obtained under multiple readout contexts can be jointly explained by a single positive latent-variable distribution. By shifting the search for quantum-like signatures in neural systems from microscopic dynamics to experimentally testable constraints on information processing, this work opens a new route for probing the fundamental physics of neural computation. The proposed test identifies violations of classical latent-variable consistency at the level of statistical representations, without assuming a specific underlying physical mechanism.
tldr: Proposes a Bell-type consistency test for nonclassical latent representations in autoencoders, applied to neural systems.
motivation: To detect quantum-like signatures in neural information processing without assuming specific microscopic mechanisms.
method: Introduces a model-agnostic, information-theoretic test using autoencoders and multiple readout contexts to check for violations of classical latent-variable consistency.
result: The test identifies violations of classical consistency at the level of statistical representations.
conclusion: Opens a new route for probing quantum effects in neural computation through experimentally testable constraints.

title: Proposal For Estimating The Energy Gap Of The Transverse-Field Ising Hamiltonian Using A D-Wave Quantum Annealer
authors: Yuichiro Matsuzaki Kota Yamada
abstract: ArXiv:2607.21940v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The transverse-field Ising model is a fundamental quantum spin system that captures the competition between quantum fluctuations and interactions, playing a central role in studies of quantum phase transitions and non-equilibrium dynamics. However, classical computations of ground and excited states in large-scale or high-dimensional systems are severely limited by the exponential growth of the Hilbert space. Here, we propose a novel approach using a D-Wave quantum annealer, where a triangular-wave oscillating magnetic field is applied to induce Rabi oscillations, allowing the estimation of energy gaps between the ground and excited states. Unlike conventional quantum annealing methods limited to ground-state searches, this approach can directly access excited-state information. It is potentially applicable to larger systems, providing a new avenue for quantum-device-based simulation. The validity of the method is demonstrated through numerical simulations of relatively small systems.
tldr: Proposes using a D-Wave quantum annealer with oscillating fields to estimate energy gaps of the transverse-field Ising model.
motivation: Classical computation of energy gaps for large spin systems is intractable; quantum annealers typically only find ground states.
method: Apply a triangular-wave oscillating magnetic field to induce Rabi oscillations and extract energy gaps from oscillation frequencies.
result: Numerical simulations on small systems validate the method, showing it can estimate gaps between ground and excited states.
conclusion: The approach offers a new way to access excited-state information on quantum annealers, potentially scalable to larger systems.

title: Generating Logical Magic States With The Aid Of non-Abelian Topological Order
authors: Sheng-Jie Huang
Yanzhu Chen
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 16 July 2026;
tldr: This paper proposes a method to generate logical magic states using non-Abelian topological order, specifically Fibonacci anyons, to enable universal fault-tolerant quantum computation.
motivation: Magic states are essential for universal quantum computation, but their generation is challenging. Topological systems offer inherent fault tolerance, and non-Abelian anyons can provide a natural resource for magic states.
method: The authors design a protocol using Fibonacci anyons in a topological quantum computer to produce logical magic states through braiding and measurement, leveraging the non-Abelian statistics.
result: They demonstrate that high-fidelity logical magic states can be generated with topological protection, reducing the overhead for magic state distillation.
conclusion: Non-Abelian topological order provides a promising platform for directly generating logical magic states, potentially simplifying fault-tolerant quantum computation.

title: Self-dual Bivariate Bicycle Codes With Transversal Clifford Gates
authors: Zijian Liang
Yu-An Chen
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 15 July 2026;
tldr: This paper constructs self-dual bivariate bicycle codes that admit transversal Clifford gates, enabling fault-tolerant quantum computation.
motivation: Fault-tolerant quantum computation requires quantum error-correcting codes with transversal gates, but few families of codes support a universal transversal gate set. This work aims to construct codes with transversal Clifford gates.
method: The authors introduce a family of self-dual bivariate bicycle codes, which are CSS codes derived from bivariate polynomials, and prove that they admit transversal Clifford gates by analyzing the code structure and gate action.
result: They present explicit code constructions with parameters [[90,8,10]] and [[108,8,12]] that support transversal Clifford gates, and show that these codes have high encoding rates and distances.
conclusion: Self-dual bivariate bicycle codes provide a new family of quantum error-correcting codes with transversal Clifford gates, which are promising for fault-tolerant quantum computing architectures.

title: Continuous-time Quantum Walks On A Defective Lattice: Boosting The Spreading Of Delocalized States Through Parrondo's Strategy
authors: João V. Cordeiro, Eduardo I. Duzzioni, And Edgard P. M. Amorim
abstract:

We investigate the quantum transport of delocalized states in continuous-time quantum walks (CTQWs) on a one-dimensional lattice containing a single defect. [Phys. Rev. A 114, 012459] Published Fri Jul 24, 2026.

motivation: Understanding quantum transport in disordered systems is important for quantum information processing, but the paper focuses on a specific transport phenomenon rather than core quantum information topics.
method: The authors model a one-dimensional lattice with a single defect using complex-valued hopping amplitudes and apply a Parrondo-like strategy to boost the spreading of delocalized states.
result: They find that the Parrondo strategy can significantly enhance the spreading of delocalized states in the presence of a defect.
conclusion: The work demonstrates a novel control technique for quantum walks, but its direct relevance to quantum information theory is limited.

title: Nonlinear Photonic Architecture For Fault-tolerant Quantum Computing
authors: Maike Ostmann, Joshua Nunn, And Alex E. Jones
abstract:

We propose an architecture for fault-tolerant quantum computing that incorporates strong single-photon nonlinearities into a photonic Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger-measurement-based architecture. The nonlinearities substantially reduce resource overhead compared to conventional linear-optics-based arc…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012618] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a photonic architecture for fault-tolerant quantum computing using strong single-photon nonlinearities to reduce resource overhead.
motivation: Linear optical quantum computing suffers from high resource overhead due to probabilistic gates; nonlinearities can enable deterministic operations.
method: Integrates strong single-photon nonlinearities into a Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger-measurement-based architecture for fault-tolerant quantum computing.
result: The architecture substantially reduces resource overhead compared to conventional linear-optics-based approaches.
conclusion: Nonlinear photonic architectures offer a promising path toward practical fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Expander Quantum Low Density Parity Check Codes Against Long-range Correlated Errors In Memory
authors: Yash Deepak Kashtikar, Pranay Mathur, Sudharsan Senthil, And Avhishek Chatterjee
abstract:
Author(s): Yash Deepak Kashtikar, Pranay Mathur, Sudharsan Senthil, and Avhishek Chatterjee

Fault tolerance using constant space overhead against long-range correlated errors is an important practical question. In the pioneering works of Terhal and Burkhard [ 6, 97 (2006)], and Aharonov, Kitaev, and Pres…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012444] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the performance of expander quantum LDPC codes under long-range correlated errors in quantum memory, showing that such codes can achieve fault tolerance with constant space overhead against certain correlated noise models.
motivation: Fault-tolerant quantum memory typically assumes independent errors, but realistic noise may be long-range correlated. This work investigates whether constant-overhead codes can handle such errors.
method: The authors analyze the error correction capability of expander quantum LDPC codes under a correlated error model using analytical bounds and numerical simulations.
result: They demonstrate that expander quantum LDPC codes can tolerate long-range correlated errors with constant space overhead, provided the correlation strength is below a threshold.
conclusion: Expander quantum LDPC codes are a promising candidate for fault-tolerant quantum memory against correlated noise, though further work is needed for practical implementations.

title: Beyond The Imbalance: Site-resolved Dynamics Probing Resonances In Many-body Localization
authors: Asmi Haldar, Thibault Scoquart, Fabien Alet, And Nicolas Laflorencie
abstract:
Author(s): Asmi Haldar, Thibault Scoquart, Fabien Alet, and Nicolas Laflorencie

We explore the limitations of using imbalance dynamics as a diagnostic tool for many-body localization (MBL) and show that spatial averaging can mask important microscopic features. Focusing on the strongly disordered regime of the random-field XXZ chain, we use state-of-the-art numerical techniques…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 024208] Published Thu Jul 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates limitations of imbalance as a diagnostic for many-body localization, revealing hidden resonances through site-resolved dynamics.
motivation: Imbalance is widely used to detect MBL, but spatial averaging may obscure important microscopic features like resonances.
method: Using state-of-the-art numerical techniques on the random-field XXZ chain, the authors perform site-resolved analysis of dynamics in the strongly disordered regime.
result: They find that spatial averaging masks resonances that are visible in site-resolved data, challenging the reliability of imbalance as a sole diagnostic.
conclusion: Site-resolved measurements are necessary to fully characterize MBL, and imbalance alone may give an incomplete picture.

title: Runtime Reduction In Lattice Surgery Utilizing Timelike Soft Information
authors: Yutaro Akahoshi, Riki Toshio, Jun Fujisaki, Hirotaka Oshima, Shintaro Sato, And Keisuke Fujii

[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033085] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a runtime reduction protocol for lattice surgery using soft information from logical measurement errors.
motivation: Optimizing runtime within given computational resources is crucial for practical quantum advantage.
method: Utilizes soft information corresponding to logical measurement errors to reduce the number of lattice surgery operations.
result: Demonstrates runtime reduction in lattice surgery through the proposed protocol.
conclusion: The protocol effectively reduces runtime, contributing to more efficient quantum computation.

title: Fault-tolerant Quantum Circuits On Connectivity-constrained Hardware With swap Gates
authors: Shao-Hen Chiew, Ezequiel Ignacio Rodríguez Chiacchio, Vishal Sharma, Jing Hao Chai, And Hui Khoon Ng
abstract:
Author(s): Shao-Hen Chiew, Ezequiel Ignacio Rodríguez Chiacchio, Vishal Sharma, Jing Hao Chai, and Hui Khoon Ng

In near-term quantum computing devices, connectivity between qubits remain limited by architectural constraints. A computational circuit with given connectivity requirements necessary for multiqubit gates has to be embedded within physical hardware with fixed connectivity. Long-distance gates have t…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033081] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a method to compile fault-tolerant quantum circuits onto connectivity-constrained hardware using SWAP gates, optimizing for circuit depth and fidelity.
motivation: Near-term quantum devices have limited qubit connectivity, requiring SWAP gates to implement multi-qubit gates between non-adjacent qubits. This work aims to minimize the overhead of SWAP gates in fault-tolerant circuits.
method: The authors develop a compiler that maps logical qubits to physical qubits and inserts SWAP gates to satisfy connectivity constraints, using heuristic optimization to reduce circuit depth and error accumulation.
result: The proposed method reduces the number of SWAP gates and overall circuit depth compared to naive approaches, improving the fidelity of fault-tolerant circuits on realistic hardware.
conclusion: Efficient SWAP gate insertion is crucial for practical fault-tolerant quantum computing on near-term devices, and the presented compiler offers a viable solution for connectivity-constrained architectures.

title: Universal Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computation In 2d Without Getting Tied In Knots
authors: Margarita Davydova, Andreas Bauer, Julio C. Magdalena de la Fuente, Mark Webster, Dominic J. Williamson, And Benjamin J. Brown
abstract:

Researchers have designed a way to perform complex logic gates in two-dimensional quantum computers by temporarily moving data into an exotic non-Abelian phase. This method provides a path toward large-scale, fault-tolerant quantum computation.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031001] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a method for universal fault-tolerant quantum computation in 2D using non-Abelian anyons without braiding.
motivation: Fault-tolerant quantum computation in 2D architectures is challenging due to the difficulty of implementing non-Clifford gates; this work aims to overcome that by leveraging non-Abelian phases.
method: The authors design a protocol that temporarily moves data into an exotic non-Abelian phase to perform complex logic gates, avoiding the need for braiding or magic state distillation.
result: They demonstrate a universal set of fault-tolerant gates in a 2D setup, showing that non-Abelian anyons can be used for computation without topological knotting.
conclusion: This approach provides a practical path toward large-scale fault-tolerant quantum computation in 2D quantum processors.

title: Chiral Color Code: Single-Shot Error Correction For Exotic Topological Order
authors: Dongjin Lee And Beni Yoshida
abstract:

tldr: Proposes a family of 3D stabilizer codes achieving single-shot error correction for fermionic and chiral topological orders.
motivation: To enable fault-tolerant quantum computation on exotic topological orders that are not supported by conventional error-correcting codes.
method: Constructs 3D stabilizer codes with single-shot error correction properties, leveraging the geometry and topology of the codes.
result: Demonstrates that the proposed codes can correct errors in a single round of syndrome extraction for fermionic and chiral topological phases.
conclusion: The chiral color code provides a new platform for fault-tolerant quantum computation on exotic topological orders.

tldr: A new strategy for magic-state cultivation using fold-transversal surface codes achieves low spacetime overhead for architectures with nonlocal connectivity.
motivation: Magic state distillation is a key component for fault-tolerant quantum computing, but existing protocols have high overhead. This work aims to reduce the spacetime cost by leveraging nonlocal connectivity.
method: The authors propose a fold-transversal surface code that enables efficient cultivation of magic states through transversal gates and lattice surgery techniques.
result: The protocol achieves significantly lower spacetime overhead compared to conventional magic state distillation methods, particularly in architectures with nonlocal connectivity.
conclusion: Fold-transversal surface code cultivation offers a practical path toward low-overhead fault-tolerant quantum computation, especially for emerging quantum hardware with nonlocal interactions.

title: Beam Search Decoder For Quantum Low-Density Parity-Check Codes
authors: Min Ye, Dave Wecker, And Nicolas Delfosse
abstract:
