The resources are also distributed along the same organizational tree: part of the supply is available only to certain sub-trees since it is purchased for the exclusive use of certain departments or units, and some supply is available to the entire tree. We consider the allocation with multiple types of resources where there is a possibility of converting between certain pairs of resources. We formulate this allocation problem as a market equilibrium problem and derive the necessary conditions to find a feasible solution. We prove that such a feasible solution always exists and provide an algorithm to compute it. Finally, we test our algorithm on a real dataset of the allocation of computing resources, such as TPUs and GPUs at Google. Our results rely on a novel two-step process, differentiating it from previous approaches. First, we show how to solve ``easy'' (harmonic) instances of our problem that satisfy certain structural properties. Then, we show how to efficiently approximate general instances by a series of easier harmonic instances, whose solutions converge efficiently to the solution of the original problem.
tldr: This paper studies resource allocation in hierarchical organizations using market equilibrium, with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To allocate heterogeneous resources efficiently across organizational hierarchies with conversion between resource types.
method: Formulates as a market equilibrium problem, solves harmonic instances, and approximates general instances via a series of harmonic instances.
result: Proves existence of feasible solutions and provides an algorithm tested on Google's TPU/GPU allocation data.
conclusion: The two-step harmonic approximation method efficiently solves hierarchical resource allocation problems.

title: DeFiScreener: Efficient DeFi Attack Pre-screening In Smart Contracts Via Historical Case Matching
authors: Rui Cao, Shaojing Fan, Zhimei Sui, Liming Fang, Ziqi Yang, Yingying Jiao, Zhenguang Liu
abstract: ArXiv:2607.22184v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Blockchain and its killer applications, particularly decentralized finance (DeFi), are gaining widespread adoption, with over 5,200 DeFi projects deployed on mainstream blockchains as of January 2026. At the same time, security risks in DeFi are becoming increasingly serious. However, existing DeFi detection tools usually cover only specific attack types, exhibiting severely limited detection coverage. In this paper, we argue that an effective way to address this gap is to pre-screen vulnerable instances from large volumes of smart contract functions and call sequences. This is motivated by a key phenomenon we term "perilous temporal asymmetry". Inspired by this, we propose DeFiScreener, the first automated pre-screening framework for DeFi attacks that uses historical exploit cases to identify potentially vulnerable functions and call sequences. Given the full source code of a target project, DeFiScreener builds Function Call Trees (FCTs) and generates semantic embeddings for each function using a large language model (LLM), allowing both program structure and function intent to be analyzed together. It then applies a dual-level screening process. At the function level, function embeddings are matched against an Attack Pattern Library of historically exploited functions. At the sequence level, the proposed Attack Pattern Oriented Monte Carlo Tree Search (APO-MCTS) efficiently explores the FCTs and screens vulnerable call sequences. The identified candidates are ultimately passed to an LLM for further interpretive and security analysis. We empirically evaluate the DeFiScreener over datasets comprising 207 real-world DeFi attack incidents. Experimental results demonstrate that DeFiScreener achieves a remarkable 98.55% recall and 84.30% precision in attack pre-screening.
tldr: This paper presents a framework for pre-screening DeFi attacks in smart contracts using historical case matching and LLMs.
motivation: Existing DeFi detection tools cover only specific attack types, leading to limited detection coverage. The authors aim to address this by pre-screening vulnerable instances from large volumes of smart contract functions and call sequences.
method: DeFiScreener builds Function Call Trees (FCTs) from source code, generates semantic embeddings for each function using an LLM, then applies dual-level screening: function-level matching against an Attack Pattern Library and sequence-level exploration via Attack Pattern Oriented Monte Carlo Tree Search (APO-MCTS).
result: On a dataset of 207 real-world DeFi attack incidents, DeFiScreener achieves 98.55% recall and 84.30% precision in attack pre-screening.
conclusion: The proposed framework effectively pre-screens DeFi attacks with high recall and precision, demonstrating the utility of historical case matching and LLM-based embeddings for smart contract security.

title: Ice Walk Is ASP-Complete
authors: Papangkorn Apinyanon
abstract: ArXiv:2607.22224v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that the solution-search problem for the pencil puzzle Ice Walk is ASP-complete. Our reduction maps Hamiltonian cycles in an undirected maximum-degree-3 spanning subgraph of a rectangular grid graph bijectively to Ice Walk solutions.
tldr: The paper proves that the puzzle Ice Walk is ASP-complete via a reduction from Hamiltonian cycles in grid graphs.
motivation: To classify the computational complexity of the Ice Walk puzzle.
method: A polynomial-time reduction from Hamiltonian cycles in undirected maximum-degree-3 spanning subgraphs of rectangular grid graphs to Ice Walk solutions.
result: Ice Walk is ASP-complete, meaning counting solutions is as hard as counting Hamiltonian cycles.
conclusion: The puzzle is computationally hard, with implications for recreational mathematics and complexity theory.

title: trasgoDP: An Open Source Framework For Releasing Noised Tabular Microdata Under Local Differential Privacy
authors: \'alvaro L\'opez Garc\'ia Judith S\'ainz-Pardo D\'iaz
abstract: ArXiv:2607.22230v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: trasgoDP is a modular, open-source, and easy-to-use Python framework for releasing tabular microdata under {\epsilon}-local differential privacy guarantees, as well as location data under geo-indistinguishability assumptions, designed to be installed and integrated within standard data science workflows. The software enables systematic exploration of privacy-utility trade-offs across multiple mechanisms, data types, and {\epsilon} values. While differential privacy has been extensively studied for aggregate data, its application to row-wise microdata release remains underexploited in terms of reusable software tools, a gap that is even more pronounced in the case of metric privacy and location-based data. trasgoDP implements local-DP mechanisms for numerical and categorical attributes (Laplace, Gaussian, Exponential, and Randomized Response), a geo-indistinguishability mechanism for location data, and a set of utility metrics, including a novel correlation-loss measure, to quantify information loss as a function of the allocated privacy budget. The objective of this work is to provide the research community with a reproducible, open-source baseline for evaluating tabular and location-based data publication methodologies under formal local differential privacy guarantees.
tldr: This paper presents an open-source Python framework for releasing tabular microdata under local differential privacy and geo-indistinguishability.
motivation: There is a lack of reusable software tools for releasing row-wise microdata under local differential privacy, especially for location data.
method: The framework implements local-DP mechanisms (Laplace, Gaussian, Exponential, Randomized Response) and a geo-indistinguishability mechanism, along with utility metrics including a novel correlation-loss measure.
result: The framework enables systematic exploration of privacy-utility trade-offs across multiple mechanisms, data types, and epsilon values.
conclusion: The work provides a reproducible, open-source baseline for evaluating tabular and location-based data publication methodologies under formal local differential privacy guarantees.

title: Kalyna Block Cipher: From Design Space Exploration To Asic Design
authors: Carlos Gewehr, Levent Aksoy, Mariia Rodinko, Roman Oliynykov, Samuel Pagliarini
abstract: ArXiv:2607.22269v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Kalyna block cipher is a Ukrainian cryptography standard, selected through a national competition held between 2007 and 2010 and approved in 2015. Although its software implementations have been introduced, hardware-efficient implementations of the algorithm, i.e., accelerators, do not exist. In this paper, we explore various design architectures to implement its encryption, decryption, and unified encryption/decryption functions, considering the trade-off between area and latency. We present hardware reduction techniques and introduce alternative designs with low area, latency, and energy consumption, targeting an application-specific integrated circuit (ASIC). We present hardware-efficient designs that include countermeasures against side-channel analysis (SCA) and fault injection (FI) attacks, such as hiding, masking, and duplication techniques. We validate these implementations in a 65\;nm ASIC chip. Experimental results confirm the need for alternative designs that explore the design search space for different requirements. The proposed architectures enable hiding the power SCA leakage by randomizing the execution of operations, and the temporal duplication in designs with countermeasures against the SCA attacks can mitigate the FI attacks. The functionality of the ASIC test chip, including various Kalyna designs, is validated through measurements.
tldr: This paper presents hardware-efficient ASIC implementations of the Kalyna block cipher with side-channel and fault injection countermeasures.
motivation: Hardware-efficient implementations of the Kalyna block cipher, a Ukrainian national standard, were lacking; the paper aims to fill this gap by exploring design architectures and countermeasures.
method: The authors explore various design architectures for encryption, decryption, and unified functions, applying hardware reduction techniques and countermeasures like hiding, masking, and duplication, then validate on a 65nm ASIC chip.
result: Experimental results confirm the trade-offs between area, latency, and energy, and show that the proposed designs can mitigate power SCA and FI attacks.
conclusion: The paper provides a set of hardware-efficient Kalyna designs with security countermeasures, validated on an ASIC chip, offering options for different requirements.

title: Three-player Differential Game Logic
authors: Andr\'e Platzer Julia Butte
abstract: ArXiv:2607.22359v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper introduces the three-player differential game logic dGL3, which enables the verification of hybrid games of discrete and differential equation dynamics with three players who may or may not form coalitions. Each player has an individual goal they try to fulfill, so the game becomes non-zero-sum when the goals of the players overlap. This enables dGL3 to verify complex situations involving multiple players, taking into account their coalitional power. dGL3 excels at verifying games where players share safety objectives but otherwise pursue different goals, so that they may or may not collaborate. In this case, zero-sum assumptions lead to overly conservative results by neglecting the potential of coordination amongst the players. In this paper, the syntax and semantics of dGL3 are presented and crucial properties of dGL3 are proved. A sound and relatively complete proof calculus for dGL3 is introduced and the use of dGL3 is illustrated in a canonical example.
tldr: This paper introduces a three-player differential game logic for verifying hybrid games with non-zero-sum objectives.
motivation: Existing verification methods for hybrid games assume zero-sum or two-player settings, which are insufficient for multi-player scenarios where players may cooperate or have overlapping goals.
method: The authors define the syntax and semantics of dGL3, a differential game logic for three players, and present a sound and relatively complete proof calculus.
result: The logic enables verification of hybrid games with three players and coalitional dynamics, illustrated with a canonical example.
conclusion: dGL3 extends hybrid game verification to multi-player non-zero-sum settings, providing a foundation for analyzing complex interactions.

title: Machine-Checked Arithmetic Bit Complexity Of The Kannan-Bachem Smith Normal Form In Lean 4
authors: Junye Ji
abstract: ArXiv:2607.22524v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We formalize in Lean 4 the Kannan-Bachem Smith normal form algorithm for nonsingular square integer matrices. The program returns [MATH] and proves [MATH], [MATH], four inverse identities, the Smith divisibility conditions, and equality of [MATH] with a canonical reference matrix. Stabilization terminates because each recursive pass strictly decreases the binary size of the active pivot; the outer algorithm recurses on the lower-right block. The computation also emits a flat trace of designated sign-magnitude arithmetic leaves. Branch conditions, quotients, Bezout data, and matrix entries are taken from the recorded primitive runs. Composite phases form their traces by concatenating the charge lists returned by the executed children. Verified self-delimiting codecs define the input and output sizes. Coefficient and work recurrences, closed by a kernel-checked polynomial-envelope calculus, give fixed polynomial bounds for both trace cost and the encoded length of the five output matrices. The theorem concerns these arithmetic primitives; structural operations and compiled Lean runtime are outside the model.
tldr: This paper formalizes the Kannan-Bachem Smith normal form algorithm in Lean 4, focusing on arithmetic bit complexity and formal verification.
motivation: To provide a machine-checked proof of correctness and complexity bounds for a classical algorithm in integer matrix theory.
method: The algorithm is implemented in Lean 4 with recursive stabilization, trace recording of arithmetic operations, and polynomial-envelope calculus for complexity bounds.
result: The formalization proves correctness, divisibility conditions, and fixed polynomial bounds for trace cost and output size.
conclusion: The work contributes to formal verification of algorithms but has no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: What Ai Red-Team Evaluations Can And Cannot Prove
authors: Bandana Kaur
abstract: ArXiv:2607.21735v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Red-team evaluations of AI models support some claims and not others, and the boundary between the two is calculable rather than merely a matter of judgment. We define the evidential ceiling of an evaluation as the largest factor by which one result can move belief under a fixed testing budget, derive it in closed form for the benchmark null result, and use it to locate that boundary exactly. We find that above a calculable harm rate, a benchmark of modest size certifies a category to a stated evidentiary standard, and a clean sheet is then the stronger of the two possible observations, outweighing a single reproduced failure. Below that rate, no passive benchmark of feasible size provides the specified evidence of safety under the fixed scoring rule and approximately independent trial structure. The crossing between the two regimes has a closed form. The bound is not specific to benchmarks: written in terms of a procedure's hypothesis conditioned elicitation rates, it covers adaptive and automated red teaming as well, and shows that discrimination between the hypotheses rather than attack success is what determines evidential worth. Auditing eight evaluation suites against the boundary, we find that current benchmarks are adequate for high-frequency harm categories and several orders of magnitude short for rare, catastrophic ones. Safety benchmarks are not uninformative. They are informative about a specific and computable set of propositions, and the discipline they need is to state which.
tldr: This paper analyzes the evidential limits of AI red-team evaluations, deriving a bound on the evidence they can provide for safety claims.
motivation: To clarify what conclusions can and cannot be drawn from red-team evaluations of AI models, especially for rare catastrophic harms.
method: The author defines the evidential ceiling of an evaluation, derives it in closed form for benchmark null results, and audits eight evaluation suites against this boundary.
result: Current benchmarks are adequate for high-frequency harms but orders of magnitude short for rare catastrophic harms; a clean sheet can be stronger than a single reproduced failure above a calculable harm rate.
conclusion: Safety benchmarks are informative about specific propositions, and the field needs to state which propositions they address.

title: Physiological Signals As A Forensic Modality For Talking-Face Deepfake Detection
authors: Tamer Aldwairi Othmane Harraq
abstract: ArXiv:2607.21776v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Talking-face (TF) deepfake generation synthesizes photore- alistic facial video from a static source image and an au- dio signal, producing forgeries that current image-based detectors consistently fail to identify. Unlike face-swap ma- nipulation, TF synthesis has no underlying real video from which to inherit physiological characteristics, making re- mote photoplethysmography (rPPG) a uniquely motivated detection modality for this forgery category. We propose a detection framework that extracts per-video rPPG wave- forms via RhythmFormer and trains a suite of lightweight classifiers to distinguish real from synthesized physiologi- cal signals. Evaluated on the TF subset of Celeb-DF++ un- der a strict subject-independent protocol, where test identi- ties are completely separated from training identities, our 1D ResNet achieves an AUC of 0.806 and EER of 27.8%, placing it within 2.4 points of the best published general- purpose detector (Effort, ICML 2025) while operating ex- clusively on the physiological channel. We document a con- trolled reproduction study of DeepFakesON-Phys, the rep- resentative prior rPPG detector, demonstrating degrada- tion from AUC 0.999 on legacy face-swap data to 0.622 on the TF subset of Celeb-DF++. We further show that detec- tion difficulty is strongly method-dependent: AUC ranges from 0.985 (Real3DPortrait) to 0.690 (IP-LAP) across the seven TF generators, with the ranking remaining perfectly stable across all evaluation protocols. This spread reflects an interpretable physiological property of each generator rather than evaluation noise, and constitutes the primary theoretical contribution of the work.
tldr: This paper uses remote photoplethysmography (rPPG) to detect talking-face deepfakes, focusing on physiological signal analysis rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: Talking-face deepfakes are hard to detect with image-based methods; rPPG offers a physiological detection modality.
method: Extracts rPPG waveforms using RhythmFormer and trains lightweight classifiers (e.g., 1D ResNet) to distinguish real from fake signals.
result: Achieves AUC 0.806 and EER 27.8% on Celeb-DF++ TF subset; detection difficulty varies across generators.
conclusion: rPPG-based detection is viable but less effective than general-purpose detectors; physiological interpretability is a key contribution.

title: Probing Speaker Identity Sensitivity In Audio Deepfake Detectors
authors: Arun Ross Daniyal Kabir Dar
abstract: ArXiv:2607.21820v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Audio deepfake detectors are trained to distinguish genuine speech from synthetic speech and often perform well on standard benchmarks. Yet the same detector that achieves less than 1% error on one dataset can see its error rate increase twentyfold when evaluated on a different dataset. We argue that one contributing factor is speaker-identity reliance: standard training corpora correlate speaker identity with the genuine/synthetic label, allowing detectors to partially rely on speaker-related cues rather than synthesis artifacts alone. We propose the Identity Sensitivity Score (ISS), a per-utterance diagnostic that quantifies how much a detector's output changes across different speaker identity contexts. ISS requires no ground-truth labels at inference time and can be computed from the detector score and a pool of reference speaker examples. Across two detectors and two datasets, incorrectly classified utterances have ISS scores 29 to 52 times higher than correctly classified utterances, and ISS alone predicts misclassification with area-under-curve (AUC) up to 0.954. To test whether ISS actually captures identity-sensitive behavior rather than serving only as a proxy for prediction confidence, we apply voice conversion to 500 utterances and measure the resulting detector-score shift. Utterances flagged as identity-sensitive by ISS respond 19 to 30 times more strongly to this manipulation than utterances flagged as stable. These results position ISS as a practical inference-time diagnostic for speaker-dependent failure analysis in audio deepfake detection.
tldr: This paper proposes an Identity Sensitivity Score (ISS) to diagnose speaker-identity reliance in audio deepfake detectors.
motivation: Audio deepfake detectors often fail on new datasets; the authors hypothesize that detectors rely on speaker identity cues correlated with genuine/synthetic labels, rather than synthesis artifacts.
method: The Identity Sensitivity Score (ISS) quantifies how much a detector's output changes across different speaker identity contexts, computed from the detector score and a pool of reference speaker examples without ground-truth labels.
result: Incorrectly classified utterances have ISS scores 29–52 times higher than correct ones; ISS predicts misclassification with AUC up to 0.954; voice conversion experiments confirm ISS captures identity-sensitive behavior.
conclusion: ISS is a practical inference-time diagnostic for speaker-dependent failure analysis in audio deepfake detection.

title: No Snake Oil: Verifying Python Package Builds
authors: Jens Dietrich, Spencer Sun, Tim W. White, Behnaz Hassanshahi
abstract: ArXiv:2607.21888v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Python has become the default language for interacting with AI, with packages being distributed through registries like the Python Package Index (PyPI). This creates a need to analyse supply chains comprising such packages. One such analysis is to rebuild packages in order to identify compromised builds injecting malware. Independent rebuilds in hardened environments have the added advantage that they can generate and record provenance in order to increase the trustworthiness of packages. Two tools that are designed to automate such rebuilds and run them at scale are macaron and oss-rebuild. We study 12,180 popular releases from PyPI and find that the byte-for-byte equivalence rate is generally low. We analyse the reasons why they produce different wheels, and find that equivalence between the original and rebuilt wheels can often still be established, preserving most of the guarantees users expect from rebuildable releases. We present and evaluate daleq4py, a tool to establish the equivalence of Python wheels through the kernel of a normalisation function that is based on provenance-preserving datalog rules. Experimental results show that daleq4py substantially expands the set of rebuilds that can be accepted as equivalent. Although only 15.4% of macaron rebuilds and 19.1% of oss-rebuild rebuilds are byte-for-byte identical to the published PyPI wheels, daleq4py establishes wheel equivalence for 60.2% and 78.9% of source-equivalent rebuilds, respectively.
tldr: This paper studies the reproducibility of Python package builds from PyPI, analyzing why byte-for-byte equivalence fails and proposing a normalization tool to establish equivalence.
motivation: Python packages are widely used in AI and other domains, but compromised builds can inject malware. Verifying that a package's source code matches its distributed wheel is crucial for supply chain security.
method: The authors rebuild 12,180 popular PyPI releases using two automated rebuild tools (macaron and oss-rebuild), analyze the causes of byte-for-byte differences, and develop daleq4py, a tool that uses datalog rules to normalize wheels and establish equivalence.
result: Only 15.4% of macaron and 19.1% of oss-rebuild rebuilds are byte-for-byte identical, but daleq4py establishes wheel equivalence for 60.2% and 78.9% of source-equivalent rebuilds, respectively.
conclusion: While byte-for-byte reproducibility is low, equivalence can often be established through normalization, preserving trust guarantees for most rebuildable releases.

title: ISPCloak: Weaponizing Isp For Optimization-Free Physical Camouflage Against Deepfake Detectors
authors: Jiale Zhao, Jiajun Wan, Lei Tang, Ye Qin, Kebing Jin, Jinghui Qin
abstract: ArXiv:2607.21897v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The rapid advancement of generative models has spurred the critical need to evaluate the worst-case robustness of deepfake detectors. In this paper, we reveal a fundamental blind spot in current forensic paradigms: while existing detectors excel at capturing digital synthesis artifacts, their effectiveness drops drastically when AI-generated content is cloaked in authentic physical imaging characteristics. We posit that genuine photographs inherently possess hardware-intrinsic statistical signatures, which are imperceptible footprints imprinted by optical sensors and Image Signal Processing (ISP) pipelines, and are fundamentally absent in purely data-driven generative models. Driven by this insight, we propose ISPCloak, a novel optimization-free adversarial attack framework that explicitly weaponizes the ISP pipeline to mislead the judgment of deepfake detectors. Rather than relying on computationally expensive gradient perturbations, our method first employs an Invertible ISP network to project images into the RAW domain. Then, we seamlessly imprint the complex statistical priors of real cameras onto AI-generated images by injecting realistic Poisson-Gaussian sensor noise and conducting forward ISP reconstruction. Synergized with generative artifact suppression and adaptive masking, this streamlined physical simulation enables ultra-fast generation of adversarial examples. Extensive experiments show that embedding authentic physical perturbations fundamentally disrupts a broad range of current detection mechanisms, yielding universally evasive adversarial examples with imperceptible visual alterations.
tldr: This paper proposes ISPCloak, an optimization-free adversarial attack that exploits ISP pipelines to create physical camouflage evading deepfake detectors.
motivation: Current deepfake detectors fail when AI-generated images are cloaked with authentic physical imaging characteristics, revealing a blind spot in forensic paradigms.
method: The method uses an invertible ISP network to project images to RAW domain, injects realistic Poisson-Gaussian sensor noise, and performs forward ISP reconstruction to imprint hardware-intrinsic statistical signatures.
result: Extensive experiments show that embedding authentic physical perturbations disrupts a broad range of detection mechanisms, yielding universally evasive adversarial examples with imperceptible visual alterations.
conclusion: The work highlights the need for forensic detectors to account for physical imaging signatures to maintain robustness against such attacks.

title: Siren (Luring LLMs Onto The Rocks): PAIR-Driven Preference Manipulation In Web-RAG Recommenders
authors: Evan Caville, Siamak Layeghy, Billy Sung, Sara Dolnicar, Marius Portmann
abstract: ArXiv:2607.21951v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This paper investigates the adversarial manipulation of the ranked recommendations produced by web-augmented large language models (LLMs). When an LLM answers a recommendation query by retrieving and reading live webpages, it acts as a recommender, and each retrieved page becomes a potential attack surface. Prior work has examined fabricated products, retrieval poisoning, and rank promotion. However, these studies do not compare how different edits to an already retrieved page change the model's final ranking while the surrounding source set remains unchanged. To address this gap, we propose SIREN, an automated attacker--judge method that adapts the PAIR jailbreaking loop to competitive rank manipulation, with the goal of moving a chosen entity to rank~1 in an LLM-generated recommendation. SIREN retrieves and captures webpages using Anthropic's web tools, then iteratively edits a retrieved source using an interpretable taxonomy of 23 content-poisoning techniques. The custom-RAG replay platform keeps the same sources in the same order, so changes in the model's ranking can be linked to changes in the supplied content rather than to differences in retrieval. Across two production Claude models, SIREN reaches rank~1 in 62 of 124 technique trials nested within eight query--model contexts. The payloads that reached rank~1 were then tested in fresh sessions, where they reproduced the result with a mean success rate of 0.805. Across the evaluated settings, declarative ranking claims and seeded lists were generally more effective than directive-form injections, although the strength of this difference depended on the target model. To the best of our knowledge, this is among the first controlled studies of competitive rank manipulation in production LLMs where the supplied source context is kept fixed.
tldr: This paper studies adversarial manipulation of LLM-based web-augmented recommenders using a PAIR-driven method to promote a target entity to rank 1.
motivation: Prior work on manipulating LLM recommendations did not isolate the effect of content edits on ranking while keeping the retrieved source set fixed.
method: SIREN adapts the PAIR jailbreaking loop to iteratively edit a retrieved webpage using 23 content-poisoning techniques, with a custom RAG replay platform to control for retrieval variation.
result: In experiments with two Claude models, SIREN achieved rank 1 in 62 of 124 trials, and payloads reproduced the result in fresh sessions with mean success rate 0.805.
conclusion: Declarative ranking claims and seeded lists are generally more effective than directive injections, but effectiveness depends on the target model.

title: KaPilot: LLM-Assisted Generation Of Kani Specifications For Unsafe Rust Verification
authors: Minghua Wang, Yuxi Ling, Mingzhi Gao, Yuwei Liu, Lin Huang
abstract: ArXiv:2607.21957v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Rust's ownership and type system provide strong memory safety guarantees, but unsafe code still presents memory safety risks. Formal verification is crucial for ensuring memory safety, but writing precise specifications for unsafe Rust is challenging and largely manual. Large language models (LLMs) have shown promise in generating formal specifications but are often code-centric, prone to inheriting implementation flaws, and lack systematic quality assessment. In this paper, we present KaPilot, a multi-agent framework for automatically generating specifications to verify unsafe Rust memory safety using Kani. The process begins with lightweight program analysis and proof harness generation. The SafetyReq agent extracts a concise, refined list of safety requirements from the target Rust function's documentation, which guides the SpecGenerate agent in producing initial specifications that specify memory safety concerns. Then, the specifications are iteratively refined through a generate-precheck-verify loop involving SpecGenerate, SpecPrecheck, and SpecVerify agents, which assess quality and feed errors back. By executing this loop multiple times, KaPilot generates a set of candidate specifications. Finally, the shuffle-and-implication strategy is applied to systematically determine the best specification from these candidates. We evaluated KaPilot on 54 unsafe Rust functions with ground truth and 70 without. KaPilot achieved 88.9% and 71.4% specification generation success, respectively, with 57.4% of generated specifications equivalent to or stronger than the ground truth. Compared with AutoSpec, KaPilot produces 14.8% more verifiable specifications and 25.9% more equivalent-or-better specifications.
tldr: This paper presents a multi-agent LLM framework for generating formal specifications to verify memory safety in unsafe Rust code using the Kani verifier.
motivation: Writing precise specifications for unsafe Rust is challenging and manual; LLMs can help but often produce flawed specifications.
method: KaPilot uses a multi-agent system with SafetyReq, SpecGenerate, SpecPrecheck, and SpecVerify agents in a generate-precheck-verify loop, followed by a shuffle-and-implication strategy to select the best specification.
result: On 54 unsafe Rust functions with ground truth, KaPilot achieved 88.9% specification generation success, with 57.4% of generated specifications equivalent to or stronger than ground truth.
conclusion: KaPilot improves over existing methods like AutoSpec in generating verifiable and correct specifications for unsafe Rust memory safety.

authors: Ruohan Zhong
Jinjun Xue

abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 27 July 2026;
tldr: This paper introduces an Energy Engel Coefficient using food-related energy consumption to identify poverty in rural China.
motivation: Traditional income-based poverty measures may miss low-income households; a new indicator based on energy consumption could reveal hidden poverty.
method: Using household survey data from China, the authors compute the Energy Engel Coefficient and compare it with income-based measures.
result: The Energy Engel Coefficient identifies low-income rural households not captured by traditional income-based poverty measures.
conclusion: Food-related energy consumption is a useful complementary indicator for poverty identification in rural China.

method: The authors report a 'twist-expand-seal' strategy involving sequential ring expansion and cyclization reactions to form cyclic biaryls with adjustable ring sizes.
result: They successfully synthesized a series of cyclic biaryls with high enantioselectivity and conformational constraint.
conclusion: The twist-expand-seal strategy provides a new approach to access structurally unique biaryl compounds with potential applications in drug discovery and chiral materials.

motivation: Diabetes impairs bone healing due to disrupted mechanical homeostasis; the authors aim to develop a material that restores the local viscoelastic environment.

result: ViscoClamp restores bone-forming activity under diabetic stress and improves jaw and skull bone repair in rats.

result: Microbial drought resistance strategies shift under aridity, and aridification amplifies their effects on soil carbon loss.
conclusion: Microbial adaptation to drought comes at the cost of increased soil carbon mineralization, which has implications for carbon cycling in drylands.

tldr: This paper studies colloidal transport and filtration in porous media using microfluidic experiments and simulations, focusing on flow-induced intermittent transport.

conclusion: The findings challenge single-collector models and highlight the need to incorporate intermittent transport for accurate filtration predictions.

method: The authors develop a theoretical model incorporating fitness effects to derive scaling laws between mRNA and protein levels.
result: They find that the scaling exponent is determined by the relative fitness contributions of mRNA and protein, providing a quantitative explanation for observed correlations.
conclusion: The work offers an evolutionary rationale for mRNA-protein correlation, improving the interpretation of transcriptomic data in terms of protein abundance.

motivation: Understanding the distribution of baryons in the universe is a key goal of cosmology, and FRBs provide a unique probe of diffuse plasma.
method: The authors cross-correlate the dispersion measures of FRBs from the CHIME/FRB catalog with the positions of foreground galaxies from a galaxy survey.
result: They detect a significant cross-power spectrum signal, indicating that FRB dispersion measures trace the large-scale structure of galaxies.
conclusion: FRBs can be used as effective tracers of the cosmic web, and future surveys will improve constraints on baryon distribution.

The complicated morphology of these waveforms due to …

motivation: Eccentric binary mergers are astrophysically important but computationally expensive to model, hindering their inclusion in gravitational-wave searches.
method: The authors propose a paradigm that chases orbital parameters rather than time, enabling efficient surrogate modeling of eccentric waveforms over long durations.
result: The method significantly reduces computational cost while maintaining accuracy, making eccentric template generation feasible for current detectors.
conclusion: This work enables routine inclusion of eccentricity in gravitational-wave data analysis, improving astrophysical interpretation of compact binary mergers.

method: The authors develop a Bayesian framework for combining heterogeneous PTA datasets, accounting for common noise processes and correlated signals.
result: The combined analysis yields a higher signal-to-noise ratio and more precise characterization of the gravitational wave background compared to individual analyses.
conclusion: Data combination is a powerful tool for PTA science, and the proposed method can be applied to future datasets.

tldr: This paper studies radiation reaction effects on coherent emission in relativistic magnetized shocks, which is a topic in astrophysics and plasma physics, not quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: Relativistic magnetized shocks are potential sources of fast radio bursts (FRBs), and understanding radiation reaction effects is crucial for modeling their emission.
method: The authors theoretically analyze the impact of radiation reaction on particle dynamics and coherent emission in magnetized shocks.
result: Radiation reaction significantly alters particle dynamics and the resulting coherent emission spectrum.
conclusion: Radiation reaction must be accounted for in models of coherent emission from relativistic magnetized shocks to accurately predict FRB properties.

title: Four Regimes Of Primary Radiation Damage In Tungsten
authors: J. Byggmästar, V-M. Yli-Suutala, A. Fellman, J. Åström, J. Westerholm, And F. Granberg

motivation: Tungsten is a critical plasma-facing material in fusion reactors, and understanding radiation damage is essential for reactor design.
method: Large-scale molecular dynamics simulations of collision cascades in tungsten were performed to observe defect production across different energy regimes.
result: Four distinct regimes of primary damage were identified, including a linear regime at high energies, which was observed for the first time in silico.
conclusion: The results provide a comprehensive picture of radiation damage in tungsten, aiding in the prediction of material performance under fusion conditions.

method: Perspective article summarizing current understanding and future directions in high-energy-density physics.

title: Fundamentals Of Vacuum Breakdown In High-gradient Accelerator Structures
authors: Walter Wuensch, Sergio Calatroni, Flyura Djurabekova, Andreas Kyritsakis, And Yinon Ashkenazy
abstract:
Author(s): Walter Wuensch, Sergio Calatroni, Flyura Djurabekova, Andreas Kyritsakis, and Yinon Ashkenazy

Vacuum breakdown or arcing happens when a very strong electric field causes a metal surface in a vacuum to suddenly form plasma, allowing large electrical currents to flow. Breakdown can damage particle accelerators, fusion reactors, satellites, and x-ray devices, though it is useful in technologies like plasma thrusters. Scientists have studied this unpredictable and fast phenomenon for over a century. Recent advances in experiments and computer simulations now provide a coherent mechanistic picture: tiny surface defects, electrical stress, heat, and emitted particles interact in complex ways to trigger breakdowns. These insights could improve high-power technologies and make advanced accelerators more reliable and efficient.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025004] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper reviews the physics of vacuum breakdown in high-gradient accelerator structures, focusing on the role of surface defects, electrical stress, and plasma formation.
motivation: Vacuum breakdown limits the performance of particle accelerators, fusion reactors, and other high-voltage devices; understanding its mechanism is crucial for improving reliability and efficiency.
method: The authors synthesize experimental observations and computer simulations to build a coherent mechanistic picture of the breakdown process, from defect initiation to plasma formation.
result: They identify that tiny surface defects, electrical stress, heat, and emitted particles interact in complex ways to trigger breakdowns, providing a unified explanation for the phenomenon.
conclusion: These insights can guide the design of more robust accelerator structures and other high-power technologies, potentially enabling more reliable and efficient advanced accelerators.

title: Colloquium: Hadron Production In Open-charm Meson Pairs At ${e}^{+}{e}^{−}$ Colliders
authors: Xiongfei Wang, Xiang Liu, And Yuanning Gao
abstract:
Author(s): Xiongfei Wang, Xiang Liu, and Yuanning Gao

Hadron spectroscopy is a frontier of particle physics; searching for new hadrons is crucial for validating the theory of strong interaction (QCD). Investigating how charmonium, a bound state of charm and anticharm quarks, decays and searching for new charmoniumlike states yield valuable insights into strong interaction mechanisms, including quark confinement and gluon binding. Hadrons produced at e− collisions decaying to open-charm meson pairs are a primary source of experimental information for these investigations. This Colloquium reviews current progress from BARBAR, Belle, CLEO-c, and BESIII experiments. As BESIII accumulates high-precision data, it has emerged as the leading facility for measuring hadron production in charm-meson pair systems, and recent advances are highlighted.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 021001] Published Fri Apr 03, 2026.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews hadron production in open-charm meson pairs at e+e- colliders, focusing on charmonium spectroscopy and strong interaction mechanisms.
motivation: Searching for new hadrons and understanding charmonium decays provides insights into quantum chromodynamics, quark confinement, and gluon binding.
method: The paper reviews experimental progress from BESIII, BaBar, Belle, and CLEO-c, highlighting measurements of hadron production in charm-meson pair systems.
result: BESIII has emerged as the leading facility for such measurements, with recent high-precision data advancing the field.
conclusion: Continued study of open-charm meson pairs will further validate QCD and may reveal new hadronic states.

authors: Michael C. Nolan, Lynn M. Carter, And Edgard G. Rivera-Valentín
abstract:
Author(s): Michael C. Nolan, Lynn M. Carter, and Edgard G. Rivera-Valentín

For more than two decades, the planetary radar installed at the Arecibo Telescope was the most sensitive instrument of its kind, harnessing the penetrating power of radio waves to perform observations of the (sub)surface of planets, moons, and asteroids in the Solar System—providing a unique perspective on those bodies that helped to drive in situ exploration. This Colloquium presents an overview of the scientific legacy of the Arecibo radar system, focusing on the period posterior to the Gregorian Update in the late 1990s until the unexpected demise of the telescope in 2020. After recalling the basics of planetary radar techniques, it reviews key Arecibo observations of Mercury, Venus, Mars, our Moon, and the Saturn system, and highlights its essential role in the characterization of a large sample of near-Earth asteroids and comets.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 011003] Published Tue Mar 31, 2026.
tldr: This colloquium reviews the scientific legacy of planetary radar at the Arecibo Observatory, focusing on observations of solar system bodies.
motivation: Planetary radar provides unique subsurface and surface information about planets, moons, and asteroids, complementing in situ exploration.
method: The paper summarizes the basics of planetary radar techniques and reviews key Arecibo observations of Mercury, Venus, Mars, the Moon, the Saturn system, and near-Earth asteroids and comets.
result: Arecibo's planetary radar was the most sensitive instrument of its kind for over two decades, enabling detailed characterization of many solar system objects.
conclusion: The Arecibo radar system made significant contributions to planetary science, and its loss marks the end of an era for ground-based radar astronomy.

title: Colloquium: Radio Astronomy With The Arecibo 305-m Telescope: In Contemporaneous Context
authors: Tapasi Ghosh And Chris Salter
abstract:
Author(s): Tapasi Ghosh and Chris Salter

The Arecibo Observatory, inaugurated in 1963 as the world’s largest single-dish radio telescope, remained at the forefront of astronomy and atmospheric science for more than five decades, until its catastrophic collapse in December 2020. This Colloquium focuses on Arecibo’s enduring legacy in radio astronomy, offering a historical perspective that emphasizes how successive major upgrades of the telescope continuously expanded its observational capabilities and scientific impact. It presents Arecibo’s most influential contributions in topics as diverse as pulsar studies, the mapping of neutral hydrogen (HI) in the Milky Way and other galaxies, the characterization of the interstellar medium, the imaging of extragalactic radio sources with very long baseline interferometry (VLBI), the search for extraterrestrial intelligence (SETI), and being a major contributor to the first-ever detection of a stochastic gravitational-wave background.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 011004] Published Tue Mar 31, 2026.
tldr: A historical review of the Arecibo radio telescope's contributions to radio astronomy and atmospheric science.
motivation: To document the legacy of the Arecibo Observatory and its impact on various fields of astronomy.
method: Historical narrative and summary of key scientific results from Arecibo's operations and upgrades.
result: Arecibo made influential contributions to pulsar studies, HI mapping, VLBI, SETI, and gravitational-wave detection.
conclusion: Arecibo's unique capabilities and upgrades enabled groundbreaking discoveries over five decades.

title: Colloquium: Geospace Pathfinder Science At Arecibo Observatory
authors: J. D. Mathews, M. P. Sulzer, And Shikha Raizada
abstract:
Author(s): J. D. Mathews, M. P. Sulzer, and Shikha Raizada

The Arecibo Observatory housed the largest single-aperture radio telescope for approximately 50 years. A major scientific focus was studying the upper atmosphere; its highly sensitive radar facility, combined with lidars, optical sensors, and satellite-based systems, enabled unprecedented studies of ionospheric physics based on incoherent scattering of radio waves off free electrons. After establishing the fundamental concepts and observables of the incoherent scattering radar technique, this Colloquium reviews key advances obtained with the Arecibo suite of instruments in multiple areas of geospace science, including plasma physics, space weather, lidar studies of atomic metals in the ionosphere, and ionosphere-magnetosphere coupling.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 011005] Published Tue Mar 31, 2026.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews geospace science advances made using the Arecibo Observatory's radar and lidar instruments, focusing on ionospheric physics and space weather.
motivation: The Arecibo Observatory's unique capabilities for studying the upper atmosphere and ionosphere have led to significant advances in geospace science, which are summarized here.
method: The paper reviews the incoherent scatter radar technique and presents key findings from Arecibo's suite of instruments, including lidars and optical sensors, in studying plasma physics, space weather, and ionosphere-magnetosphere coupling.
result: The review highlights advances in understanding ionospheric plasma processes, atomic metal layers, and coupling between the ionosphere and magnetosphere.
conclusion: The Arecibo Observatory has been instrumental in advancing geospace science, and its legacy continues through the data and insights obtained.

title: Colloquium: Multimessenger Astronomy With Continuous Gravitational Waves And Future Detectors
authors: Benjamin J. Owen
abstract:
Author(s): Benjamin J. Owen

The search for continuous gravitational waves from rotating neutron stars represents a key frontier of gravitational-wave astrophysics, with strong connections to electromagnetic astronomy, nuclear astrophysics, and condensed matter physics. This Colloquium discusses the detection prospects for these long-lived yet elusive signals in the upcoming generation of gravitational-wave detectors, emphasizing the importance of simultaneous electromagnetic observations. It also surveys the potential implications of such multimessenger observations for our understanding of the physical and astrophysical processes taking place in the extremely dense environments of their sources.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 011002] Published Tue Mar 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper discusses multimessenger astronomy with continuous gravitational waves from rotating neutron stars, focusing on detection prospects and astrophysical implications.
motivation: Continuous gravitational waves from neutron stars are a key frontier in gravitational-wave astrophysics, with connections to electromagnetic astronomy and nuclear astrophysics.
method: The paper reviews detection prospects for future gravitational-wave detectors and emphasizes simultaneous electromagnetic observations.
result: It surveys potential implications for understanding physical processes in dense neutron star environments.
conclusion: Multimessenger observations with continuous gravitational waves will enhance our understanding of neutron star physics.

title: Colloquium: Convection-cloud Chambers: Experiment And Theory
authors: Steven Krueger And Raymond A. Shaw
abstract:
Author(s): Steven Krueger and Raymond A. Shaw

In warm clouds, drops grow into raindrops through both condensation and collision coalescence, but the observed rapid transition between these mechanisms remains difficult to theoretically explain. The convection-cloud chamber, which reproduces key phenomena such as turbulent fluctuations in droplet concentrations and supersaturation under controlled laboratory conditions, offers a promising approach to addressing this long-standing bottleneck in understanding in cloud physics. This Colloquium reviews the physics underlying the precipitation bottleneck, examines how convection-cloud chambers capture the essential processes, and synthesizes insights from experiments, theory, and computational models that bridge laboratory and atmospheric scales.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 011001] Published Wed Feb 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper reviews convection-cloud chambers as a laboratory tool to study the precipitation bottleneck in warm clouds.
motivation: Understanding the rapid transition from condensation to collision-coalescence in warm clouds is a long-standing problem in cloud physics.
method: The authors review experimental, theoretical, and computational studies using convection-cloud chambers that reproduce key cloud phenomena under controlled conditions.
result: Convection-cloud chambers can capture essential processes like turbulent fluctuations in droplet concentration and supersaturation, bridging laboratory and atmospheric scales.
conclusion: The convection-cloud chamber is a promising approach to address the precipitation bottleneck, but the paper does not contribute to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Colloquium: Gravitational Waves From Neutrino-driven Core Collapse Supernovae
authors: A. Mezzacappa And M. Zanolin
abstract:
Author(s): A. Mezzacappa and M. Zanolin

The observation of a core collapse supernova explosion of (near-)Galactic origin would constitute a landmark, once-in-a-century event for multimessenger astronomy, eagerly awaited by observers and modelers alike. The detection of gravitational waves, along with photons and neutrinos, from such an event would provide unique insights into the supernova central engine and the physics of the newly forming neutron star. This Colloquium presents the latest progress in core collapse supernova modeling and the associated gravitational wave signal predictions. It also provides an overview of the specific methods of detection and physical parameter estimation that can be implemented for such signals in ground-based laser interferometers, in the context of multimessenger research strategies.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 041002] Published Tue Dec 30, 2025.
tldr: This colloquium reviews gravitational wave signals from core collapse supernovae and their detection methods.
motivation: Observing a Galactic core collapse supernova would provide unique multimessenger insights into the supernova engine and neutron star formation.
method: The paper summarizes recent progress in supernova modeling and gravitational wave signal predictions, and discusses detection and parameter estimation techniques for ground-based laser interferometers.
result: The review presents the current state of gravitational wave predictions from core collapse supernovae and outlines multimessenger observation strategies.
conclusion: Gravitational wave detection from a nearby supernova would significantly advance our understanding of the explosion mechanism and neutron star physics.

title: Colloquium: The Cosmic Dipole Anomaly
authors: Nathan Secrest, Sebastian von Hausegger, Mohamed Rameez, Roya Mohayaee, And Subir Sarkar
abstract:
Author(s): Nathan Secrest, Sebastian von Hausegger, Mohamed Rameez, Roya Mohayaee, and Subir Sarkar

The cosmological principle, which states that the Universe must be statistically isotropic and homogeneous on large scales, is a foundational principle of the standard model of cosmology, known as lambda cold dark matter (ΛCDM). The validity of this principle can be tested by assessing the compatibility of a dipole anisotropy in the large-scale distribution of matter with the dipole observed in the cosmic microwave background, interpreted in the ΛCDM model as due to our local peculiar motion. This Colloquium describes the methodology for such a test and presents its outcome based on the analysis of recent large catalogs of radio galaxies and quasars, revealing a significant inconsistency between the two dipoles. The authors review these recent findings, as well as potential biases, systematic issues, and alternate interpretations, and discuss how this anomaly could challenge the standard description of our Universe based on the ΛCDM model.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 041001] Published Thu Dec 11, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews the cosmic dipole anomaly, testing the cosmological principle by comparing the dipole in the large-scale matter distribution with the CMB dipole.
motivation: To test the foundational cosmological principle of isotropy and homogeneity by examining a potential inconsistency between the matter dipole and the CMB dipole.
method: Analysis of recent large catalogs of radio galaxies and quasars to measure the dipole anisotropy and compare it with the CMB dipole, including assessment of biases and systematic issues.
result: A significant inconsistency is found between the two dipoles, challenging the standard ΛCDM model.
conclusion: The cosmic dipole anomaly may indicate a violation of the cosmological principle or require modifications to the standard model of cosmology.

title: Astrophysical Tests Of Dark Matter Self-interactions
authors: Susmita Adhikari, Arka Banerjee, Kimberly K. Boddy, Francis-Yan Cyr-Racine, Harry Desmond, Cora Dvorkin, Bhuvnesh Jain, Felix Kahlhoefer, Manoj Kaplinghat, Anna Nierenberg, Annika H. G. Peter, Andrew Robertson, Jeremy Sakstein, And Jesús Zavala
abstract:
Author(s): Susmita Adhikari, Arka Banerjee, Kimberly K. Boddy, Francis-Yan Cyr-Racine, Harry Desmond, Cora Dvorkin, Bhuvnesh Jain, Felix Kahlhoefer, Manoj Kaplinghat, Anna Nierenberg, Annika H. G. Peter, Andrew Robertson, Jeremy Sakstein, and Jesús Zavala

Dark sectors, involving new particles that couple very weakly to the standard model ones, play an important role in current model-building efforts in particle physics, as they allow, for example, for new dark matter production and interaction mechanisms. This review focuses on self-interacting dark matter scenarios, their implications on the dynamics and distribution of dark matter halos in the Universe, and the related astrophysical tests and observations, from galaxies to large-scale structures. It is embedded in the framework of the Novel Probes Project, a forum connecting observers and theorists involved in the study of astrophysical tests of dark-sector interactions.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045004] Published Mon Dec 08, 2025.
tldr: A review of astrophysical tests of dark matter self-interactions, focusing on dark sector models and their observational signatures.
motivation: To understand the properties of dark matter beyond the collisionless cold dark matter paradigm by exploring self-interacting dark matter scenarios.
method: Review of theoretical models and astrophysical observations from galaxies to large-scale structures, including simulations and data comparisons.
result: Summarizes current constraints on dark matter self-interaction cross sections and outlines future observational prospects.
conclusion: Self-interacting dark matter remains a viable extension of the standard model, with ongoing and future surveys expected to provide tighter constraints.

title: Prospects For Supersymmetry At High-Luminosity Lhc
authors: Howard Baer, Vernon Barger, Jessica Bolich, Juhi Dutta, Dakotah Martinez, Shadman Salam, Dibyashree Sengupta, And Kairui Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Howard Baer, Vernon Barger, Jessica Bolich, Juhi Dutta, Dakotah Martinez, Shadman Salam, Dibyashree Sengupta, and Kairui Zhang

Supersymmetry remains one of the leading candidates for physics beyond the standard model, offering a compelling framework to address the hierarchy of scales. Its theoretical appeal has inspired decades of intensive model building and experimental searches. Recent results have placed stringent bounds on the supersymmetric parameter space, sharpening the focus on the remaining viable models. This review surveys the current status and outlook for supersymmetry in light of experimental constraints and recent theoretical developments, and presents projections for the discovery potential of the High-Luminosity Large Hadron Collider across multiple search channels and a variety of well-motivated scenarios.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045001] Published Fri Oct 17, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews the prospects for supersymmetry at the High-Luminosity LHC, focusing on experimental searches and model constraints.
motivation: Supersymmetry is a leading candidate for physics beyond the Standard Model, but recent experimental results have constrained its parameter space, motivating a survey of viable models and future discovery potential.
method: The authors survey current experimental constraints and theoretical developments, and project discovery potential across multiple search channels at the HL-LHC.
result: The paper provides an overview of the status of supersymmetry and outlines the remaining viable scenarios that could be probed at the HL-LHC.
conclusion: Supersymmetry remains a compelling framework, and the HL-LHC offers significant discovery potential for well-motivated models.

title: Solar Fusion Iii: New Data And Theory For Hydrogen-burning Stars
authors: B. Acharya et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): B. Acharya et al.

Approximately 90% of the stars in the Milky Way are on the main sequence, fusing hydrogen into helium through a network of nuclear reactions. This includes the nearest star, our Sun. A precise understanding of hydrogen burning is crucial to predicting its luminosity, neutrino production, and helioseismology. This review describes the theoretical and experimental work of the last decade that has advanced our understanding of the nuclear physics of hydrogen burning. It describes the plasma and atomic physics that influences the solar environment in which the nuclear reactions take place, as well as the diagnostics probes—including solar neutrinos and helioseismology—that allow us to test our resulting model of the solar interior.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 035002] Published Thu Sep 04, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews nuclear physics of hydrogen burning in stars, focusing on solar fusion reactions, plasma physics, and diagnostics like neutrinos and helioseismology.
motivation: Understanding hydrogen burning is crucial for predicting stellar properties such as luminosity, neutrino production, and helioseismology.
method: The review synthesizes theoretical and experimental advances over the last decade in nuclear reaction rates, plasma and atomic physics, and solar interior modeling.
result: Updated nuclear reaction rates and improved solar models are presented, with comparisons to neutrino and helioseismic data.
conclusion: The new data and theory refine our understanding of solar fusion, but the paper does not address quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Quantum Physics Of Stars
authors: M. Wiescher, C. A. Bertulani, C. R. Brune, R. J. Deboer, A. Diaz-Torres, L. R. Gasques, K. Langanke, P. Navrátil, W. Nazarewicz, J. Okołowicz, D. R. Phillips, M. Płoszajczak, S. Quaglioni, And A. Tumino
abstract:
Author(s): M. Wiescher, C. A. Bertulani, C. R. Brune, R. J. deBoer, A. Diaz-Torres, L. R. Gasques, K. Langanke, P. Navrátil, W. Nazarewicz, J. Okołowicz, D. R. Phillips, M. Płoszajczak, S. Quaglioni, and A. Tumino

There are many nuclear reactions that are of central importance for stellar burning and element formation. In typical stars, these reactions take place at very low energy, and many of them have very small rates, making it difficult to measure them directly in the laboratory. On the theoretical side, the low-energy regime is governed by quantum-mechanical phenomena like tunneling, near-threshold resonances, and interference effects. This review summarizes the state of the art in the theory of low-energy nuclear reactions in stars and describes new ideas for studying these reactions on Earth.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025003] Published Tue May 27, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews the quantum mechanical phenomena underlying low-energy nuclear reactions in stars, such as tunneling and resonances.
motivation: Understanding nuclear reactions at stellar energies is crucial for stellar burning and nucleosynthesis, but direct measurements are often impossible due to extremely small reaction rates.
method: The authors summarize the state-of-the-art theoretical framework for low-energy nuclear reactions, including quantum tunneling, near-threshold resonances, and interference effects, and discuss new experimental approaches.
result: The review provides a comprehensive overview of theoretical models and experimental techniques for studying stellar nuclear reactions.
conclusion: Advances in theory and experiment are enabling better understanding of stellar nucleosynthesis, but the paper does not contribute to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Codata Recommended Values Of The Fundamental Physical Constants: 2022
authors: Peter J. Mohr, David B. Newell, Barry N. Taylor, And Eite Tiesinga
abstract:
Author(s): Peter J. Mohr, David B. Newell, Barry N. Taylor, and Eite Tiesinga

This review contains the 2022 self-consistent set of values of the constants and conversion factors of physics and chemistry recommended by the Committee on Data for Science and Technology (CODATA). The CODATA values are based on a least-squares adjustment that takes into account all data available up to the end of 2022. Details of the data selection and methodology are described.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025002] Published Wed Apr 30, 2025.

motivation: Accurate and consistent values of fundamental constants are essential for science and technology.

result: A self-consistent set of values and conversion factors for physics and chemistry.
conclusion: The updated CODATA values provide the most accurate and reliable constants for 2022.

title: Gas Bubble Dynamics
authors: Dominique Legendre And Roberto Zenit
abstract:
Author(s): Dominique Legendre and Roberto Zenit

The motion of gas bubbles in liquids plays a vital role in numerous natural, industrial, and everyday phenomena. Unlike solid particles, gas bubbles are nearly weightless and highly responsive to forces from the surrounding fluid. Their dynamics are affected by added mass acceleration and deformable surfaces, and also by interactions with turbulent flows, other bubbles, and walls, with liquid rheology and surfactants further influencing their behavior. This review examines the intricate behavior of noncondensable gas bubbles, highlighting key advances over the past 20 years. Key topics include turbulence, non-Newtonian fluids, and electrolytes, offering insights to enhance modeling and guide future research in two-phase flow systems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025001] Published Thu Apr 17, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews the dynamics of gas bubbles in liquids, covering turbulence, non-Newtonian fluids, and electrolytes.
motivation: Understanding gas bubble dynamics is important for many natural and industrial processes, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The review synthesizes advances over the past 20 years, focusing on key topics such as turbulence, non-Newtonian fluids, and electrolytes.
result: The paper highlights key advances and offers insights to enhance modeling and guide future research in two-phase flow systems.
conclusion: The review provides a comprehensive overview of gas bubble dynamics but is unrelated to the user's research interests.

title: The Need For Optoacoustic Microscopy
authors: Ludwig Englert, Dominik Jüstel, And Vasilis Ntziachristos
abstract:
Author(s): Ludwig Englert, Dominik Jüstel, and Vasilis Ntziachristos

Advanced imaging methods are essential for providing biological and clinical insight into cells and biological tissues. Optoacoustic imaging is one such method in which cells or tissues absorb short laser pulses and the resulting rise in temperature creates tiny ultrasound waves that can be detected by ultrasonic detectors placed outside the specimen. This noninvasive technique has the ability to look at optical contrast that is millimeters and even centimeters deep with high resolution. This review discusses the basic physics, how the method impacts biological and clinical research, and the latest developments in multimodal microscopy and imaging combining optical and optoacoustic techniques.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015005] Published Tue Mar 04, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews optoacoustic microscopy, a biomedical imaging technique that uses laser pulses to generate ultrasound waves for deep-tissue imaging.
motivation: Advanced imaging methods are needed for biological and clinical insight; optoacoustic imaging offers high-resolution, deep-tissue optical contrast noninvasively.
method: The review covers the basic physics of optoacoustic signal generation, detection, and multimodal microscopy combining optical and optoacoustic techniques.
result: Optoacoustic microscopy enables imaging at millimeter-to-centimeter depths with high resolution, impacting biological and clinical research.
conclusion: Optoacoustic microscopy is a valuable tool for biological imaging, with ongoing developments in multimodal approaches.

title: Wrinkles, Creases, And Cusps In Growing Soft Matter
authors: Martine Ben Amar
abstract:
Author(s): Martine Ben Amar

The buckling of a material surface subject to compression or growth is a ubiquitous phenomenon, arising in materials science contexts such as the swelling of gels as well as in biological contexts such as morphogenesis and embryogenesis. A complete understanding of the creases and sharp cusps that commonly accompany buckling requires nonlinear elasticity theory. This review presents a modern treatment of the Biot instability, integrating many standard techniques of nonlinear physics and solid mechanics, such as bifurcation theory, conformal mapping, and
[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015004] Published Mon Feb 24, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews nonlinear elasticity theory for buckling, creases, and cusps in growing soft matter, with applications in materials science and biology.
motivation: Understanding the formation of creases and cusps during buckling of soft materials is important for morphogenesis and swelling of gels.
method: The review integrates techniques from nonlinear physics and solid mechanics, including bifurcation theory, conformal mapping, and elliptic integrals.

title: Hierarchically Discriminating Haar-randomness In Quantum States From A Black-box Device
authors: Hao Wang And Adrián Pérez-Salinas Xavier Bonet-Monroig
abstract: The concept of randomness in quantum computing has been central to constructing benchmarking tools, cryptographic protocols, as well as a proof of beyond-classical computation. Discerning whether quantum states (or unitaries) are randomly distributed is a computational task that requires an enormous amount of quantum computational resources. This work addresses such a challenge by introducing a hierarchical discrimination algorithm to efficiently test if a set of states generated from a black-box quantum device with an unknown distribution is (in)compatible with a random distribution. To this end, we reduce the complexity of the problem by selecting an observable with known spectrum to study the statistical properties of its expectation values with respect to the quantum states from an unknown (black-box) quantum device. Concurrently, we use our first technical result, a connection between Haar-randomness and the Dirichlet distribution, to analytically compute Haar-random moments of the observable. Our Haar-random discriminator test is then simply to compare those statistical moments, such that if fails the test, it is enough to state that the quantum device does not output randomly distributed states. Else, we can not (yet) confirm that the states follow a Haar-random distribution. We further provide an extension to this algorithm by permutation- and unitary-equivalent randomization of the observable at increasing computational resources, which allows us to more accurately state whether is compatible with Haar-randomness. We envision the use of the discriminator test as a quantum device benchmark, by discriminating whether the states generated are incompatible with Haar-randomness.
tldr: Analysis failed

title: Broadband High-gain Metalens Design Based On Dispersion Compensation
authors: Yanwei Wang, Chuanfei Li, Zhuo Liu And Yunsheng Guo
abstract: Broadband metasurface focusing is often limited by unit-cell phase dispersion and phase–amplitude coupling, leading to degraded performance near the band edges in conventional geometrical-optics (GO) designs. To address this challenge, an inverse-design method combining an artificial neural network and particle swarm optimization is proposed. The unit-cell response is modeled in the complex domain to avoid phase-wrapping discontinuities, while a frequency-dependent aperture reference phase is globally optimized to balance phase accuracy and transmittance. Based on this method, a broadband metalens operating from 9.0 to 10.2 GHz (12.5%) is designed and fabricated. Measured results agree well with simulations and demonstrate a gain enhancement of up to 4.36 dBi over a conventional GO design, with a peak gain of 23.8 dBi. Compared with the feed antenna alone, the maximum gain improvement reaches 16.05 dBi, while the half-power beamwidth is reduced by up to at 10.2 GHz. The proposed method provides an effective route for broadband high-gain metalens design under practical unit-cell constraints.
tldr: This paper presents an inverse-design method for broadband high-gain metalens antennas using neural networks and particle swarm optimization.
motivation: Broadband metasurface focusing is limited by unit-cell phase dispersion and phase-amplitude coupling, degrading performance near band edges in conventional designs.
method: An artificial neural network models the unit-cell response in the complex domain to avoid phase-wrapping discontinuities, and particle swarm optimization globally optimizes a frequency-dependent aperture reference phase.
result: A metalens operating from 9.0 to 10.2 GHz achieves up to 4.36 dBi gain enhancement over conventional design, with peak gain of 23.8 dBi and reduced half-power beamwidth.
conclusion: The proposed method provides an effective route for broadband high-gain metalens design under practical unit-cell constraints.

title: Steady-state Entanglement Harvesting For Two Rotating Atoms In A Cylindrical Cavity
authors: Hong-Tao Zheng, Xiang-Fa Zhou, Guang-Can Guo And Zheng-Wei Zhou
abstract: We study the entanglement dynamics of two rotating atoms (with two internal levels and ) in a cylindrical cavity, which interact with a massless scalar field in vacuum satisfying the Dirichlet boundary condition. Our analysis demonstrates that it is possible to obtain the steady-state entanglement under two types of resonant conditions. For two identical atoms with the same world-line, the system reduces to the usual dissipative Dicke model at the first resonant condition where and are the energy splitting and the angular velocity of the th atom, and is the Lorentz factor. The entangled steady-state takes the form where and are constant, which is consistent with the previous study (see 2022 Phys. Rev. D 106 105028). For two atoms with different world-lines, the system suffers from a significant mixed joint dissipation process at the second resonant condition , and reaches an entangled steady-state as . Moreover, with the help of the cavity, we can obtain a much higher concurrence in the final states by changing the relative ratio of the two orbital radii. Our work thus provides a more effective way for the extraction of steady-state entanglement from the vacuum via the analogue Unruh effect for two rotating atoms in a cylindrical cavity.
